sentences.zh: 于栗磾，代人也。

translations.literal: Yu Lidi was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lidi came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少習武藝，材力過人，能左右馳射。

translations.literal: In youth he trained in martial arts; his strength surpassed others, and he could shoot while galloping to either side.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he trained in arms; his strength outmatched others, and he could shoot from horseback at full gallop.

sentences.zh: 登國中，拜冠軍將軍，假新安子。

translations.literal: In the Dengguo era he was appointed Champion General and made Acting Lord of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dengguo period he was made Champion General and Acting Lord of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 與甯朔將軍公孫蘭，潛自太原，從韓信故道，開井陘關路，襲慕容寶於中山。

translations.literal: With Pacifier of the North General Gongsun Lan he secretly left Taiyuan, followed Han Xin's old route, opened the Jingxing Pass road, and raided Murong Bao at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: With Pacifier of the North Gongsun Lan he stole out of Taiyuan, took Han Xin's old road, opened the Jingxing route, and struck Murong Bao at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 道武后至，見道路修理，大悅，即賜其名馬。

translations.literal: Daowu arrived later, saw the roads repaired, and was greatly pleased; he at once bestowed famous horses upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu came afterward, saw the roads in order, and was delighted; he immediately gave him renowned horses.

sentences.zh: 及趙魏平，帝置酒高會，謂栗磾曰：「卿，吾之黥、彭也！

translations.literal: When Zhao and Wei were pacified, the Emperor set out wine at a great gathering and said to Lidi, "You are my Ying and Peng!
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao and Wei were subdued, the Emperor held a great feast and told Lidi, "You are my Ying Bu and Peng Yue!

sentences.zh: 」進假新安公。

translations.literal: " He was advanced to Acting Duke of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Duke of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 道武田于白登山，見熊將數子，顧栗磾曰：「能搏之乎？

translations.literal: Daowu hunted at White Deer Mountain, saw a bear with several cubs, turned to Lidi and said, "Can you wrestle it?
translations.idiomatic: Daowu was hunting on White Deer Mountain, saw a bear with cubs, and asked Lidi, "Can you grapple with it?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「若搏之不勝，豈不虛斃一壯士！

translations.literal: " He replied, "If I wrestle and do not win, would I not have killed a stalwart in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Lidi answered, "If I fight and fail, I would waste a brave man for nothing!

sentences.zh: 自可驅致御前，坐而制之。

translations.literal: I can simply drive it to the imperial presence and control it while seated.
translations.idiomatic: Better to drive it before Your Majesty and subdue it at a distance.

sentences.zh: 」尋皆禽獲，帝顧而謝之。

translations.literal: " Before long all were captured alive; the Emperor turned and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all were taken alive; the Emperor turned and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 後為河內鎮將。

translations.literal: Later he became Garrison Commander of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Garrison Commander of Henei.

sentences.zh: 劉裕之伐姚泓，栗磾慮北侵擾，築壘河上。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, Lidi feared northern raids and built fortifications along the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu marched against Yao Hong, Lidi feared incursions from the north and built riverbank fortifications.

sentences.zh: 裕憚之，遺栗磾書，假道西上。

translations.literal: Yu feared him and sent Lidi a letter asking passage westward.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was wary of him and wrote Lidi requesting a corridor west.

sentences.zh: 題書曰：「黑槊公麾下」。

translations.literal: The letter was addressed, "Under the Black Spear Duke."
translations.idiomatic: The superscription read, "To the Black Spear Duke's command."

sentences.zh: 栗磾以狀表聞，明元因之授栗磾黑槊將軍。

translations.literal: Lidi reported the matter; Mingyuan thereupon appointed Lidi General of the Black Spear.
translations.idiomatic: Lidi memorialized the court; Mingyuan then made him General of the Black Spear.

sentences.zh: 栗磾好持黑槊，裕望而異之，故有其號。

translations.literal: Lidi loved to carry a black spear; Yu saw it from afar and marveled, hence the title.
translations.idiomatic: Lidi favored a black spear; Yu glimpsed it from afar and was struck by it, hence the name.

sentences.zh: 遷豫州刺史，進爵新安侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Yuzhou and advanced to Marquis of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Inspector of Yuzhou and raised to Marquis of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 洛陽雖歷代所都，實為邊界，栗磾勞來安集，甚得百姓心。

translations.literal: Luoyang, though a capital of successive dynasties, was in truth a frontier; Lidi labored to settle and comfort the people and won their hearts deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had been many dynasties' capital yet lay on the border; Lidi worked to settle the people and won them wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 明元南幸盟津，謂栗磾曰：「河可橋乎？

translations.literal: Mingyuan traveled south to Meng Ford and asked Lidi, "Can the river be bridged?
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan went south to Meng Ford and asked Lidi, "Can we bridge the river?

sentences.zh: 」栗磾曰：「杜預造橋，遺事可想。

translations.literal: " Lidi said, "Du Yu built a bridge—one may think on that precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Lidi said, "Du Yu once bridged it; the precedent still stands.

sentences.zh: 」乃編大船，構橋於野阪。

translations.literal: " He then lashed great boats and built a bridge at Wild Slope.
translations.idiomatic: He moored great boats and threw a bridge across at Wild Slope.

sentences.zh: 六軍既濟，帝深歎美之。

translations.literal: When the six armies had crossed, the Emperor sighed in deep admiration.
translations.idiomatic: After the six armies crossed, the Emperor marveled aloud.

sentences.zh: 太武之征赫連昌，敕栗磾與宋兵將軍周幾襲陝城，長驅至三輔。

translations.literal: When Taiwu campaigned against Helian Chang, he ordered Lidi and Song General Zhou Ji to strike Shancheng and drive deep into the Three Metropolises region.
translations.idiomatic: On Taiwu's campaign against Helian Chang, Lidi and Song General Zhou Ji were sent to take Shancheng and press into the heartland.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 累遷外都大官，平刑折獄，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Officer of the Outer Court; in judging criminal cases he won great renown.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Grand Officer of the Outer Court and won fame for fair judgment.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 栗磾自少總戎，迄于白首，臨事善斷，所向無前。

translations.literal: Lidi from youth commanded armies until white-haired age; in affairs he judged well and wherever he went none stood before him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to white hair Lidi held command; he decided swiftly in the field and none could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 加以謙虛下士，刑罰不濫，太武甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: Moreover he was humble toward scholars and did not abuse punishments; Taiwu deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He was moreover modest toward men of worth and sparing in punishment; Taiwu grieved deeply for him.

sentences.zh: 子洛拔，有姿容，善應對。

translations.literal: His son Luoba was handsome in bearing and skilled in repartee.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luoba was handsome and quick in speech.

sentences.zh: 拜侍御中散。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Imperial Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant Imperial Scribe.

sentences.zh: 太武甚加愛寵，因賜名焉。

translations.literal: Taiwu greatly favored him and therefore bestowed the name upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu doted on him and gave him the name Luoba.

sentences.zh: 轉監禦曹令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Imperial Wardrobe Office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Supervisor of the Imperial Wardrobe Office.

sentences.zh: 景穆在東宮，厚加禮遇。

translations.literal: Jingmu was in the Eastern Palace and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jingmu in the Eastern Palace honored him warmly.

sentences.zh: 洛拔恆畏避摒退，不敢逆自結納。

translations.literal: Luoba always feared and avoided drawing near, not daring to court favor on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Luoba always held back and shunned advance, not daring to court favor himself.

sentences.zh: 頃之，襲爵。

translations.literal: Before long he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 後為侍中、尚書令，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: Later he was Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat; the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat; officials stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 洛拔有六子。

translations.literal: Luoba had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: Luoba had six sons.

sentences.zh: 長子烈，善射，少言，有不可犯之色。

translations.literal: The eldest, Lie, was skilled in archery, spoke little, and had a countenance none might offend.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Lie, excelled at archery, spoke little, and wore a face none dared cross.

sentences.zh: 少拜羽林中郎，累遷侍中、殿中尚書。

translations.literal: In youth he was appointed Cadet of the Feathered Forest; he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Young he entered the Feathered Forest; he rose to Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 于時孝文幼沖，文明太后稱制。

translations.literal: At that time Xiaowen was young and Empress Dowager Wenming held the regency.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen was still a child and Empress Dowager Wenming ruled in his name.

sentences.zh: 烈與元丕、陸睿、李沖等各賜金策，許以有罪不死。

translations.literal: Lie, with Yuan Pi, Lu Rui, Li Chong, and others each received a golden tally granting that crimes would not bring death.
translations.idiomatic: Lie, Yuan Pi, Lu Rui, Li Chong, and others each received a golden tally promising immunity from capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 進爵洛陽侯，轉衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Marquis of Luoyang and transferred to Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Marquis of Luoyang and Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 及遷都洛陽，人情戀本，多有異議。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, people's hearts clung to the old home and many objected.
translations.idiomatic: At the transfer to Luoyang many clung to the old capital and murmured against it.

sentences.zh: 帝以問烈。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Lie.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor questioned Lie.

sentences.zh: 曰：「陛下聖略深遠，非愚管所測。

translations.literal: He said, "Your Majesty's sacred design is far-reaching—not something a fool may measure.
translations.idiomatic: Lie said, "Your Majesty's design is too deep for a fool to fathom.

sentences.zh: 若隱心而言，樂遷之與戀舊，中半耳。

translations.literal: If I speak from the heart, those glad to move and those longing for the old are about half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking honestly, delight in the move and longing for the old divide the people evenly.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿不唱異同，朕深感不言之益。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "You do not lead the opposition; I deeply feel the benefit of your silence.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You do not stir dissent; I value deeply what you leave unsaid.

sentences.zh: 」敕鎮代，留台庶政，一相參委。

translations.literal: He was ordered to garrison Dai while routine affairs of the rear capital were all referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to hold Dai; routine government at the northern capital went through him.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸代，執烈手曰：「宗廟至重，翼衛不輕。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Dai, he took Lie's hand and said, "The ancestral temple is weightiest; its guard is no light charge.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial visit to Dai the Emperor took Lie's hand and said, "The ancestral temple is paramount; guarding it is no small trust.

sentences.zh: 卿當祗奉靈駕，時遷洛邑。

translations.literal: You should reverently escort the spirit tablets and come to Luoyang in due time.
translations.idiomatic: Escort the spirit tablets with reverence and join us at Luoyang in good time.

sentences.zh: 」烈與高陽王雍奉神主於洛陽，遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: Lie with Prince of Gaoyang Yong escorted the spirit lords to Luoyang and was transferred to Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Lie and Prince Yong of Gaoyang brought the spirit lords to Luoyang; he was then made Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 十九年，大選百僚，烈子登引例求進。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, in the great selection of officials, Lie's son Deng cited precedent and sought advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen, during the great selection, Lie's son Deng invoked precedent to seek promotion.

sentences.zh: 烈表引己素無教訓，請乞黜落。

translations.literal: Lie memorialized that he himself had never taught his son and asked that Deng be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Lie submitted that he had never trained his son and begged Deng's removal.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此乃有識之言，不謂烈能辨此！

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "These are words of discernment—I did not think Lie could see so clearly!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "That is the speech of a man who knows his mind—I did not expect such clarity from Lie!

sentences.zh: 」乃引見登，詔曰：「朕今創禮新邑，明揚天下，卿父乃行謙讓之表，而有直士之風，故進卿為太子翊軍校尉。

translations.literal: " He then summoned Deng and decreed, "I now establish rites in the new capital and raise men throughout the realm; your father has shown a modest memorial and the bearing of an upright man—therefore I advance you to Assistant Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Deng and said, "I am founding rites in the new capital and seeking talent across the land; your father's modest petition and upright manner move me—I advance you to Assistant Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard.

sentences.zh: 」又加烈散騎常侍，封聊城縣子。

translations.literal: " Lie was further made Regular Attendant and enfeoffed as Viscount of Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lie was also made Regular Attendant and enfeoffed Viscount of Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 及穆泰、陸睿謀反舊京，帝幸代，泰等伏法。

translations.literal: When Mu Tai and Lu Rui plotted rebellion at the old capital, the Emperor went to Dai and Tai and the rest were executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Tai and Lu Rui conspired at the old capital, the Emperor went to Dai; Tai and his fellows were put to death.

sentences.zh: 賜烈及李沖璽書，述敘金策之意。

translations.literal: Lie and Li Chong were granted imperial letters setting forth the intent of the golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: Lie and Li Chong received sealed letters reaffirming the golden tally's promise.

sentences.zh: 時代鄉舊族，同惡者多，唯烈一宗，無所染豫。

translations.literal: At that time many of the old clans of Dai shared the guilt, yet Lie's house alone was untouched.
translations.idiomatic: Many Dai clans of the day were implicated, but Lie's lineage alone stayed clean.

sentences.zh: 帝益器重之。

translations.literal: The Emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor prized him still more.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「元儼決斷威恩，深自不惡，然盡忠猛決，不如烈也。

translations.literal: He sighed and said, "Yuan Yan is decisive in authority and favor and holds himself in no low regard, yet in whole-hearted loyalty and fierce resolve he is not Lie's equal.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "Yuan Yan is sharp in reward and punishment and thinks well of himself, yet in loyal daring he falls short of Lie.

sentences.zh: 爾日烈在代都，必即斬其五三元首。

translations.literal: Had Lie been at Dai then, he would at once have beheaded the ringleaders of the Five Three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Had Lie been in Dai that day, he would have struck off the Five Three chiefs at once.

sentences.zh: 烈之節概，不謝金日磾。

translations.literal: Lie in integrity does not yield to Jin Midi.
translations.idiomatic: Lie in moral fiber does not bow to Jin Midi.

sentences.zh: 」詔除領軍將軍。

translations.literal: " He was ordered made General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 以本官從征荊沔，加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In that office he followed the campaign in Jing and Mian and was given an additional suite of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Jing and Mian in that rank and received an extra band of martial music.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，齊將陳顯達入寇馬圈，帝輿疾討之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Qi general Chen Xianda invaded Maquan; the Emperor, ill in his carriage, went to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three Chen Xianda of Qi invaded Maquan; the Emperor, sick in camp, went out against him.

sentences.zh: 執烈手，以京邑為托。

translations.literal: He took Lie's hand and entrusted the capital to him.
translations.idiomatic: He clasped Lie's hand and entrusted the capital to his care.

sentences.zh: 帝崩于行宮，彭城王勰秘諱而返。

translations.literal: The Emperor died at the traveling palace; Prince of Pengcheng Xie concealed the death and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor died on campaign; Prince Xie of Pengcheng hid the tidings and turned homeward.

sentences.zh: 稱詔召宣武會駕魯陽。

translations.literal: In the Emperor's name he summoned Xuanwu to meet the carriage at Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: He issued orders in the late Emperor's name summoning Xuanwu to join the train at Luyang.

sentences.zh: 以烈留守之重，密報凶問。

translations.literal: Because Lie's charge as defender was weighty, he secretly reported the calamitous news.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Lie's weight as defender, he secretly sent word of the death.

sentences.zh: 烈處分行留，神守無變。

translations.literal: Lie disposed the rear guard without change in spirit or bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Lie arranged the rear guard; his composure never wavered.

sentences.zh: 宣武即位，寵任如前。

translations.literal: When Xuanwu took the throne, favor toward him was as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanwu succeeded, Lie's favor stood as before.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧為宰輔，權重當時。

translations.literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi was chief minister and his power matched the age.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang was chief minister and his power dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 曾遣家僮傳言於烈，求舊羽林武賁執仗出入。

translations.literal: He once sent a household slave to speak to Lie, asking for former Feathered Forest guards to bear arms on his comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: Xi once sent a house slave to Lie requesting old Feathered Forest guards to carry arms in his train.

sentences.zh: 烈不許。

translations.literal: Lie refused.
translations.idiomatic: Lie refused.

sentences.zh: 禧遣謂烈曰：「我是天子兒，天子叔，元輔之命，與詔何異？

translations.literal: Xi sent word to Lie, "I am the Son of Heaven's son and the Son of Heaven's uncle; a chief minister's command—how does it differ from an edict?
translations.idiomatic: Xi sent word: "I am the emperor's son and uncle; a chief minister's order—how is it not an edict?

sentences.zh: 」烈厲色答曰：「向亦不道王非天子兒、叔。

translations.literal: " Lie answered sternly, "I never said Your Highness was not the Son of Heaven's son and uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Lie answered coldly, "I never denied you were the emperor's son and uncle.

sentences.zh: 若是詔，應遣官人所由。

translations.literal: If this were an edict, it should be sent through the proper officials.
translations.idiomatic: Had it been an edict, proper officers would have borne it.

sentences.zh: 若遣私奴索官家羽林，烈頭可得，羽林不可得也！

translations.literal: If you send a private slave to demand the state's Feathered Forest, you may have my head, but you will not have the guards!
translations.idiomatic: Send a private slave to seize the imperial guard, and you may have my head—but not my guards!

sentences.zh: 」禧惡烈剛直，出之為恆州刺史。

translations.literal: " Xi hated Lie's rigidity and had him sent out as Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi hated Lie's stiffness and posted him Inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 烈不願籓授，謂彭城王勰曰：「殿下忘先帝南陽之詔乎？

translations.literal: Lie did not wish a frontier appointment and said to Prince Xie of Pengcheng, "Has Your Highness forgotten the late Emperor's charge at Nanyang?
translations.idiomatic: Lie, unwilling to take a province, told Prince Xie of Pengcheng, "Have you forgotten the late Emperor's charge at Nanyang?

sentences.zh: 而逼老夫乃至於此！

translations.literal: Yet you drive an old man even to this!
translations.idiomatic: And you press an old man so far!

sentences.zh: 」遂以疾辭。

translations.literal: " He thereupon pleaded illness and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宣武以禧等專擅，潛謀廢之。

translations.literal: Xuanwu, because Xi and others monopolized power, secretly plotted to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu, seeing Xi and his faction monopolize power, secretly planned their removal.

sentences.zh: 景明二年正月，礿祭，三公致齋於廟。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Jingming, at the spring offering, the Three Dukes fasted at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jingming year two, at the spring rites, the Three Dukes kept fast at the temple.

sentences.zh: 帝夜召烈子忠謂曰：「卿父明可早入。

translations.literal: At night the Emperor summoned Lie's son Zhong and said, "Your father should come early tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Emperor called Lie's son Zhong and said, "Let your father come early tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」及明，烈至。

translations.literal: " At dawn Lie arrived.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Lie came.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「諸父慢怠，今欲使卿以兵召之，卿其行乎？

translations.literal: The decree said, "The imperial uncles are arrogant and slack; I wish you to summon them with troops—will you go?
translations.idiomatic: The edict ran, "My uncles grow insolent; I would have you summon them under arms—will you go?

sentences.zh: 」烈曰：「老臣曆奉累朝，頗以幹勇賜識。

translations.literal: " Lie said, "This old servant has served successive reigns and is known somewhat for resolve and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Lie said, "I have served many reigns and am known, if at all, for boldness.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，所不敢辭。

translations.literal: Today's affair is one I dare not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Today's task I dare not refuse.

sentences.zh: 」乃將直閣以下六十餘人，宣旨召咸陽王禧、彭城王勰、北海王詳，衛送至帝前。

translations.literal: " He then led more than sixty men including the Direct Attendants, proclaimed the intent, and summoned Prince Xi of Xianyang, Prince Xie of Pengcheng, and Prince Xiang of Beihai, escorting them to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He took sixty-odd Direct Attendants and heralds, summoned Princes Xi of Xianyang, Xie of Pengcheng, and Xiang of Beihai, and brought them before the throne.

sentences.zh: 諸公各稽首歸政。

translations.literal: Each prince bowed his head and returned his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Each bowed low and surrendered his powers.

sentences.zh: 以烈為領軍，進爵為侯，自是長直禁中，機密大事皆所參焉。

translations.literal: Lie was made General of the Guards and advanced to Marquis; from then on he held constant duty within the palace, and all weighty secrets passed through him.
translations.idiomatic: Lie became General of the Guards and Marquis; thereafter he kept constant watch in the palace and every grave secret ran through him.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧之謀反，宣武從禽於野。

translations.literal: When Prince Xi of Xianyang plotted rebellion, Xuanwu captured him in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xi of Xianyang rebelled, Xuanwu took him in the field.

sentences.zh: 左右分散，倉卒之際，莫知其計。

translations.literal: His attendants scattered; in the sudden moment none knew his plan.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants scattered; in the confusion none knew what he intended.

sentences.zh: 乃敕烈子忠馳覘虛實。

translations.literal: He then ordered Lie's son Zhong to ride out and learn the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Lie's son Zhong to ride out and learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 烈時留守，已處分有備。

translations.literal: Lie was then on garrison duty and had already made dispositions in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Lie was on garrison duty and had already made ready dispositions.

sentences.zh: 因忠奏曰：「臣雖朽邁，心力猶可。

translations.literal: Through Zhong's memorial he said, "Though I am old and failing, my heart and strength still serve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong reported Lie's words: "I am old, yet my heart and strength still hold.

sentences.zh: 禧等倡狂，不足為慮。

translations.literal: Xi and the rest are wildly reckless—not worth anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and his crew are reckless fools—not worth fear.

sentences.zh: 願緩蹕徐還，以安物望。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to return the carriage slowly and steady the people's gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty return slowly and steady the people's gaze.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚以為慰。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was greatly comforted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took great comfort from this.

sentences.zh: 車駕還宮，禧已逃，詔烈追執之。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned to the palace, Xi had already fled; the decree ordered Lie to pursue and seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the palace Xi had fled; Lie was ordered to pursue and seize him.

sentences.zh: 順後既立，以世父之重，彌見優禮。

translations.literal: After Empress Shun was established, because of his standing as paternal uncle he was treated with still greater honor.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Shun's elevation, as her father's uncle he won still finer treatment.

sentences.zh: 及卒，宣武舉哀於朝堂，給東園第一秘器，贈太尉，封钜鹿郡公。

translations.literal: At his death Xuanwu mourned him in the audience hall, granted the foremost eastern-garden funeral vessels, posthumously made him Grand Commandant, and enfeoffed him Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Xuanwu mourned in the hall, gave the finest funeral regalia, posthumously made him Grand Commandant, and enfeoffed him Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 子祚襲。

translations.literal: His son Zuo inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 祚弟忠，字思賢，本字千年。

translations.literal: Zuo's younger brother Zhong, style name Sixian, original name Qiannian.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo's younger brother Zhong, styled Sixian, had originally been named Qiannian.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，拜侍御中散。

translations.literal: At twenty he was appointed Attendant Imperial Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was Attendant Imperial Scribe.

sentences.zh: 文明太后臨朝，刑政頗峻，侍臣左右，多以微譴得罪。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, punishments were severe and attendants at the Emperor's side often fell for slight faults.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Wenming's regency justice ran harsh; many at the Emperor's side fell for trifling faults.

sentences.zh: 忠樸直少言，終無過誤。

translations.literal: Zhong was plain and upright, spoke little, and to the end made no error.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was plain, upright, and sparing of speech; he never stumbled.

sentences.zh: 太和中，授武騎侍郎，因賜名登。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was made Martial Cavalry Gentleman and therefore received the name Deng.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he became Martial Cavalry Gentleman and received the name Deng.

sentences.zh: 累遷左中郎將，領直寢。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Palace Gentleman and commanded the Direct Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Palace Gentleman and commanded the Direct Guard.

sentences.zh: 元禧之亂，車駕在外，變起倉卒。

translations.literal: At Yuan Xi's rebellion the imperial carriage was abroad and trouble rose in haste.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xi rebelled the Emperor was abroad and crisis struck in an instant.

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「臣父為領軍，計必無所慮。

translations.literal: Zhong said, "My father is General of the Guards; in his reckoning there can be no lapse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "My father commands the guards; he will have left nothing to chance.

sentences.zh: 」帝遣忠馳觀之，烈嚴備，果如所量。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Zhong to ride and see; Lie was strictly prepared, exactly as he had judged.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Zhong to look; Lie stood in full readiness, just as Zhong had said.

sentences.zh: 忠還，宣武撫其背曰：「卿差強人意。

translations.literal: When Zhong returned, Xuanwu clapped his back and said, "You are rather more than satisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong returned; Xuanwu clapped his shoulder and said, "You exceed expectation.

sentences.zh: 先帝賜卿名登，誠為美稱。

translations.literal: The late Emperor gave you the name Deng—a truly fine title.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor named you Deng—a fine name indeed.

sentences.zh: 朕嘉卿忠款，今改名忠，既表貞固之誠，亦以名實相副也。

translations.literal: I admire your loyal heart; I now rename you Zhong, both showing steadfast sincerity and matching name to reality.
translations.idiomatic: I honor your loyalty; I rename you Zhong—showing constancy and matching name to deed.

sentences.zh: 」以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning his father.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 徙為司空長史。

translations.literal: He was moved to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時太傅、錄尚書、北海王詳親尊權重，將作大匠王遇多隨詳所欲而給之。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Secretariat, Prince Xiang of Beihai, was kin to the throne and heavy in power; the Director of Palace Construction Wang Yu often supplied whatever Xiang desired.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor and Recorder Prince Xiang of Beihai was close kin and powerful; Director of Construction Wang Yu indulged his every wish.

sentences.zh: 忠於詳前謂遇曰：「殿下國之周公，阿衡王室，何至阿諛附勢，損公惠私也？

translations.literal: Before Xiang, Zhong said to Yu, "Your Highness is the state's Duke of Zhou, pillar of the royal house—how can you flatter power, harm the public good, and favor private ends?
translations.idiomatic: Before Xiang, Zhong told Yu, "Your Highness is the realm's Duke of Zhou—how can you fawn on power, wound the public good, and serve private ends?

sentences.zh: 」遇既不寧，詳亦慚謝。

translations.literal: Yu was ill at ease and Xiang also apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was uneasy; Xiang himself apologized in shame.

sentences.zh: 以平元禧功，封魏郡公。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Yuan Xi he was enfeoffed Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Yuan Xi he was enfeoffed Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 及遷散騎常侍、兼武衛將軍，每以鯁氣正辭，為北海所忿。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to Regular Attendant and concurrently Martial Guard General, he often spoke with bone and straight words, and Beihai resented him.
translations.idiomatic: As Regular Attendant and Martial Guard General he spoke with blunt bone; Beihai bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 面責忠曰：「我憂在前見爾死，不憂爾見我死時也。

translations.literal: To his face Xiang reproached Zhong, "I worry that before I die I shall see you die—not that you will see me die.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang rebuked him to his face: "I fear I shall see you die before I die—not you me.

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「人生自有定分，若應死王手，避亦不免；

translations.literal: Zhong said, "Life has its allotted portion; if I am to die by Your Highness's hand, flight will not save me.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "Each man has his fate; if I am to die by your hand, flight will not save me.

sentences.zh: 不爾，王不能殺。

translations.literal: If not, Your Highness cannot kill me.
translations.idiomatic: If not, you cannot kill me.

sentences.zh: 」詳因忠表讓之際，密勸帝以忠為列卿，於是詔停其封，優進太府卿。

translations.literal: Xiang, using Zhong's memorial of resignation as cover, secretly urged the Emperor to make Zhong a ranked minister; thereupon the decree halted his enfeoffment and favored him with advancement to Minister of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, under cover of Zhong's resignation memorial, secretly urged the Emperor to make him a ranked minister; the court stayed his enfeoffment and advanced him Minister of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 正始二年，詔忠以本官使持節、兼侍中，為西道大使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi the decree ordered Zhong, in his present office, Bearer of the Staff and Concurrent Palace Attendant, as envoy of the western circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi year two Zhong was ordered, retaining his rank, to bear the staff as Concurrent Attendant and Western Circuit envoy.

sentences.zh: 刺史、鎮將贓罪顯暴者，以狀聞。

translations.literal: Where regional inspectors and garrison commanders' crimes of graft were glaring, he reported by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Where inspectors and garrison commanders' graft was flagrant, he reported it.

sentences.zh: 守令以下，便行決斷。

translations.literal: For prefects, magistrates, and below, he executed judgment on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: For prefects, magistrates, and below, he judged and punished on the spot.

sentences.zh: 與尚書李崇分使二道。

translations.literal: He and Director of the Secretariat Li Chong divided the realm into two circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He and Director Li Chong split the realm between them.

sentences.zh: 忠劾并州刺史高聰贓罪二百餘條，論以大辟。

translations.literal: Zhong impeached Bingzhou Inspector Gao Cong on more than two hundred counts of graft and argued for the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong impeached Bingzhou Inspector Gao Cong on over two hundred counts of corruption and sought capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 除華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 遭繼母憂，不行。

translations.literal: He met with his stepmother's mourning and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother died; he did not take the post.

sentences.zh: 服闋，再遷衛尉卿、河南邑中正。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was again made Commandant of the Guard and Chief Rectifier of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he again became Commandant of the Guard and Chief Rectifier of Henan.

sentences.zh: 忠與吏部尚書元暉、度支尚書元匡、河南尹元萇等推定代方姓族。

translations.literal: Zhong with Director of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Hui, Director of Revenue Yuan Kuang, Mayor of Henan Yuan Chang, and others fixed the clan lists of the Dai region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong with Yuan Hui of Personnel, Yuan Kuang of Revenue, Yuan Chang as Mayor of Henan, and others fixed the Dai clans' registers.

sentences.zh: 高肇忌其為人，乃言于宣武，稱中山要鎮，作捍須才，乃出忠為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao resented his character and spoke to Xuanwu, saying Zhongshan was a key fortress needing a stalwart defender, and had Zhong sent out as Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao hated his manner and told Xuanwu that Zhongshan needed a strong hand; Zhong was posted Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而帝悔，復授衛尉卿、領左衛將軍、恆州大中正，密遣使詣忠，慰勉之。

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor regretted it and again appointed him Commandant of the Guard, General of the Left Guard, and Chief Rectifier of Hengzhou, secretly sending an envoy to Zhong to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Emperor repented, restored him Commandant of the Guard, General of the Left Guard, and Chief Rectifier of Hengzhou, and secretly sent envoys to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，除都官尚書，領左衛、中正如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yan chang he was made Director of the Ministry of Justice, still holding Left Guard and Chief Rectifier as before.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan chang's opening he became Director of Justice, retaining Left Guard and Chief Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 又加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was further made Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 嘗因侍宴，賜之劍杖，舉酒屬忠曰：「卿世執貞節，故恆以禁衛相委。

translations.literal: Once at a banquet he was given sword and staff; raising his cup he charged Zhong, "Your house for generations has held steadfast integrity—therefore I constantly entrust you with the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast he was given sword and staff; raising his cup he told Zhong, "Your line has held fast for generations—hence I always trust you with the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 昔以卿行忠，賜名曰忠。

translations.literal: Formerly because you acted in loyalty I gave you the name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Once, because you acted loyally, I named you Zhong.

sentences.zh: 今以卿才堪禦侮，以所禦劍杖相錫。

translations.literal: Now because your talent can repel insult I bestow these arms I carry.
translations.idiomatic: Now, seeing your talent can turn insult aside, I give you the arms at my side.

sentences.zh: 循名取義，意在不輕，出入恆以自防也。

translations.literal: Following the name to take the meaning—the intent is not light; carry them whenever you go in or out.
translations.idiomatic: Name and gift match in meaning—do not treat them lightly; bear them whenever you pass the gates.

sentences.zh: 」遷侍中、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant and General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 忠辭無學識，宣武曰：「學識有文章者不少，但心直不如卿。

translations.literal: Zhong declined for lack of learning; Xuanwu said, "Men with learning and literary polish are not few, but none has a heart as straight as yours.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong pleaded lack of scholarship; Xuanwu said, "Learned men with polished prose are plentiful, but none has your straight heart.

sentences.zh: 欲使卿劬勞於下，我當無憂於上。」

translations.literal: I wish you to labor below so that I may be without worry above."
translations.idiomatic: Labor below that I may rest above."

sentences.zh: 及帝崩夜，忠與侍中崔光遣右衛將軍侯剛迎明帝於東宮而即位。

translations.literal: On the night the Emperor died, Zhong with Palace Attendant Cui Guang sent Right Guard General Hou Gang to welcome Mingdi from the Eastern Palace to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The night the Emperor died, Zhong and Attendant Cui Guang sent Right Guard General Hou Gang to bring Mingdi from the Eastern Palace to the throne.

sentences.zh: 忠與門下議，以帝沖年，未親機政，太尉高陽王雍屬尊望重，宜入居西柏堂，省決庶政；

translations.literal: Zhong discussed with the Secretariat that the Emperor being young had not yet handled affairs himself; Grand Commandant Prince Yong of Gaoyang was kin and of heavy repute and should enter the Western Cypress Hall to decide routine government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and the Secretariat held that the boy emperor had not yet taken the reins; Grand Commandant Prince Yong of Gaoyang, eminent in kinship and name, should enter the Western Cypress Hall and decide routine affairs.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄明德茂親，可為尚書令，總攝百揆。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Rencheng was virtuous in virtue and close in kinship and could be Director of the Secretariat, overseeing the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng, virtuous and close in blood, should be Director of the Secretariat and oversee the ministries.

sentences.zh: 奏中官，請即敕授。

translations.literal: They memorialized the inner palace, asking that edicts be issued at once.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized the inner palace asking immediate edicts.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉王顯欲逞奸計，與中常侍、給事中孫蓮等厲色不聽，寢門下之奏。

translations.literal: Censor Zhongwei Wang Xian wished to carry out a treacherous plan; with Palace Secretary and Imperial Supply Officer Sun Lian and others he glared and would not listen, burying the Secretariat's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Xian plotted treachery; with Secretary Sun Lian and others he glared down the Secretariat memorial.

sentences.zh: 孫蓮等密欲矯太后令，以高肇錄尚書事，顯與高猛為侍中。

translations.literal: Sun Lian and others secretly wished to forge an order of the Empress Dowager making Gao Zhao Recorder of the Secretariat, with Xian and Gao Meng as Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lian and his circle meant to forge the Empress Dowager's order making Gao Zhao Recorder, with Xian and Gao Meng as Attendants.

sentences.zh: 忠即殿中收顯殺之。

translations.literal: Zhong at once seized Xian in the hall and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong seized Xian in the hall and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 忠既居門下，又總禁衛，遂執朝政，權傾一時。

translations.literal: Zhong, holding both the Secretariat and overall command of the guards, then grasped court power and his authority tilted the age.
translations.idiomatic: Holding Secretariat and guards together, Zhong seized the government; his power bent the age.

sentences.zh: 初，太和中，軍國多事，孝文以用不足，百官祿四分減一。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Taihe era, with many military and state affairs, Xiaowen because funds fell short cut all officials' salaries by a quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Taihe, with war and statecraft pressing, Xiaowen had cut official salaries by a quarter for lack of funds.

sentences.zh: 忠既擅朝，欲以惠澤自固，乃悉復所減之祿，職人進位一級。

translations.literal: Zhong, monopolizing the court, wished to secure himself with favor and fully restored the reduced salaries and advanced every officeholder one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Monopolizing court, Zhong sought to bind men with favor: he restored the salary cuts and raised every officer one rank.

sentences.zh: 舊制：百姓絹布一匹之外，各輸綿麻八兩。

translations.literal: The old rule: beyond one bolt of silk or cloth per commoner, each also paid eight ounces of cotton and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule, beyond one bolt of silk or cloth per household, eight ounces of cotton and hemp were due.

sentences.zh: 忠悉以與之。

translations.literal: Zhong gave all of this to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong remitted all of it to the people.

sentences.zh: 乃白高陽王雍，自雲宣武本許優轉。

translations.literal: He reported to Prince Yong of Gaoyang that Xuanwu had originally promised him preferential advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He told Prince Yong of Gaoyang that Xuanwu had promised him preferment.

sentences.zh: 雍憚忠威權，便順意加忠車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Yong feared Zhong's power and at once followed his wish, adding Zhong as General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yong feared Zhong's might and promptly made him General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 忠自謂新故之際，有安社稷功，諷百僚令加己賞。

translations.literal: Zhong deemed himself, at the turn between old and new reigns, to have merit in securing the altars and hinted that the hundred offices should increase his reward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong thought his service at the dynastic turn had saved the state and nudged officials to enlarge his reward.

sentences.zh: 太尉雍、清河王懌、廣平王懷難違其意，封忠常山郡公。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yong, Prince Yi of Qinghe, and Prince Huai of Guangping found it hard to go against his intent and enfeoffed Zhong Duke of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yong, Prince Yi of Qinghe, and Prince Huai of Guangping could not refuse; they enfeoffed him Duke of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 忠又難於獨受，乃諷朝廷，同在門下者加封邑。

translations.literal: Zhong also found it hard to accept alone and therefore hinted the court should add fiefs to those who shared the Secretariat with him.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to stand alone, he hinted that fellow Secretariat ministers should gain fiefs too.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射郭祚、尚書裴植以忠權勢日盛，勸雍出忠。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Guo Zuo and Director Pei Zhi, because Zhong's power grew daily, urged Yong to send Zhong out.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Guo Zuo and Director Pei Zhi, seeing Zhong's power swell, urged Yong to post him away.

sentences.zh: 忠聞之，逼有司誣奏其罪。

translations.literal: Zhong heard of it and forced the relevant offices to frame and impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong heard and forced the bureaus to frame charges against them.

sentences.zh: 祚有師傅舊恩，植擁地入國，忠並矯詔殺之。

translations.literal: Zuo had old favor as tutor; Zhi had brought land into the state—Zhong forged edicts and killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo had been the Emperor's tutor; Zhi had surrendered estates to the crown—Zhong forged edicts and had both killed.

sentences.zh: 朝野憤忿，無不切齒。

translations.literal: Court and country were furious; none did not gnash teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country raged; men ground their teeth.

sentences.zh: 王公以下，畏之累跡。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes downward all feared him and left tracks in heaps.
translations.idiomatic: From princes down, all feared him and crowded his path.

sentences.zh: 又欲殺高陽王雍，侍中崔光固執乃止，遂免雍太尉，以王還第。

translations.literal: He also wished to kill Prince Yong of Gaoyang; Palace Attendant Cui Guang stood firm and stopped it, and Yong was removed as Grand Commandant and sent to his estate as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: He would have killed Prince Yong; Attendant Cui Guang blocked it; Yong was stripped of Grand Commandant and sent home.

sentences.zh: 自此詔命生殺，皆出於忠。

translations.literal: From then on edicts of life and death all came from Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: From then every order of life and death issued from Zhong.

sentences.zh: 既尊靈太后為皇太后，居崇訓宮，忠為儀同三司、尚書令、崇訓衛尉，侍中、領軍如故。

translations.literal: After Empress Dowager Ling was honored as Empress Dowager and dwelt at Chongxun Palace, Zhong was made Honored Companion of the First Rank, Director of the Secretariat, Chongxun Commandant of the Guard, still Palace Attendant and General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling was honored and dwelt at Chongxun, Zhong became Honored Companion, Director of the Secretariat, Chongxun Commandant, still Attendant and General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，解忠侍中、領軍、崇訓衛尉，止為儀同、尚書令、侍中。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager held court she removed Zhong as Attendant, General of the Guards, and Chongxun Commandant, leaving him only Honored Companion, Director of the Secretariat, and Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When she took the regency she stripped him of Attendant, Guards, and Chongxun Commandant, leaving Honored Companion, Director, and Attendant.

sentences.zh: 忠為令旬余，靈太后引門下侍官，問忠在端右聲聽。

translations.literal: Zhong had been Director little more than ten days when the Empress Dowager summoned Secretariat attendants and asked how Zhong's voice and hearing were at the right hand.
translations.idiomatic: After barely ten days as Director the Empress Dowager called Secretariat officers and asked whether Zhong's conduct at her right hand was fit.

sentences.zh: 咸曰不稱厥任，乃出為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: All said he did not match his charge; he was sent out as Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: All said he failed his charge; he was posted Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 太傅清河王等奏：「忠擅殺樞納，輒廢宰輔，朝野駭心，遠近怪愕。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe and others memorialized, "Zhong on his own authority killed pivot ministers and casually deposed chief counselors; court and country were shaken, near and far astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe memorialized, "Zhong murdered key ministers and deposed chief counselors on his own authority; the realm shook.

sentences.zh: 功過相除，悉不合賞，請悉追奪。

translations.literal: Merit and fault offset each other and none of his rewards fit—we ask that all be stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Merit and crime cancel his rewards—we beg all honors be revoked.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后從之。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年，御史中尉元匡奏：「忠以鴻勳盛德，受遇累朝，幸國大災，專擅朝命，無人臣之心。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiping, Censor Zhongwei Yuan Kuang memorialized, "Zhong, for great merit and accumulated favor through many reigns, met with the state's great calamity and on his own authority held court commands—he had no heart of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping year one Censor Yuan Kuang wrote, "Zhong, favored through reigns for great deeds, used the dynastic crisis to seize commands—no subject's heart.

sentences.zh: 裴、郭受冤於既往，宰輔黜辱於明世。

translations.literal: Pei and Guo were wronged in the past; chief counselors were shamed in the bright age.
translations.idiomatic: Pei and Guo were wronged; chief ministers were disgraced in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 又自矯旨為儀同三司、尚書令、領崇訓衛尉。

translations.literal: He also on his own forged an edict making himself Honored Companion, Director of the Secretariat, and Commander of Chongxun Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He forged edicts making himself Honored Companion, Director, and Chongxun Commander.

sentences.zh: 原其此意，便欲無上自處。

translations.literal: Tracing this intent, he plainly wished to set himself above all.
translations.idiomatic: By that intent he plainly meant to stand above all.

sentences.zh: 既事在恩後，宜加顯戮。

translations.literal: Since the matter fell after the general pardon, he should receive conspicuous punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Though the general amnesty had passed, he deserved open punishment.

sentences.zh: 請遣御史一人、令史二人，就州行決。

translations.literal: We ask to send one censor, two clerks, and execute judgment at his province.
translations.idiomatic: Send one censor and two clerks to execute judgment in his province.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后令，以忠事經肆眚，遂不追罪。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered that because Zhong's affair had passed through the great pardon, punishment was not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ruled that the great pardon covered Zhong; punishment was not pursued.

sentences.zh: 又詔以忠歷任禁要，誠節皎然，賜爵靈壽縣公。

translations.literal: She also decreed that because Zhong through his posts in the inner guard had shown bright integrity, he was granted the title Duke of Lingshou.
translations.idiomatic: She also decreed that his long service in the inner guard showed bright loyalty and granted him Duke of Lingshou.

sentences.zh: 初，宣武崩後，高太后將害靈太后。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Xuanwu's death, Empress Dowager Gao was about to harm Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanwu's death, Empress Dowager Gao had plotted harm to Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 劉騰以告侯剛，剛以告忠。

translations.literal: Liu Teng told Hou Gang; Gang told Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Teng warned Hou Gang; Gang told Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠請計于崔光。

translations.literal: Zhong asked Cui Guang for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong sought Cui Guang's counsel.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「宜置胡嬪於別所，嚴兵守衛。

translations.literal: Guang said, "The Hu consorts should be placed in a separate residence with strict military guard.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "Place the Hu consorts apart under strict guard.

sentences.zh: 」忠從之，具以此意啟靈太后，太后意乃安。

translations.literal: " Zhong followed this and fully reported the intent to Empress Dowager Ling; the Empress Dowager's mind was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong obeyed, reported fully to Empress Dowager Ling, and her mind was eased.

sentences.zh: 故太后深德騰等四人，並有寵授。

translations.literal: Therefore the Empress Dowager deeply favored Teng and the other four men and all received favored appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager therefore deeply favored Teng and the other three and richly rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 忠以毀之者多，懼不免禍，願還京，欲自營救。

translations.literal: Zhong, because many slandered him, feared he could not escape disaster and wished to return to the capital to rescue himself.
translations.idiomatic: Many slandered Zhong; fearing ruin, he begged to return to the capital to save himself.

sentences.zh: 靈太后不許。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，除尚書右僕射，加侍中，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year he was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and added Palace Attendant, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, fourth month, he became Right Vice Director and Attendant, retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年三月，復儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Shengui he was again Honored Companion of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengui year one, third month, he was again Honored Companion.

sentences.zh: 疾，未拜。

translations.literal: He fell ill and did not assume the post.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill before he could take the post.

sentences.zh: 見裴、郭為祟，自知必死，先表養亡弟第二子司徒掾永超為子，乞以為嫡。

translations.literal: Seeing Pei and Guo as apparitions, he knew he must die; he first memorialized to adopt his late younger brother's second son, Registrar Yongchao of the Ministry of Works, as his heir and begged him as legitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: Haunted by visions of Pei and Guo, he knew death was near; he memorialized to adopt his late brother's second son Yongchao, a registrar of Works, as heir.

sentences.zh: 靈太后許之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager consented.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司空。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 有司奏太常少卿元端議：「案諡法，剛強理直曰武，怙威肆行曰晗鬼，宜諡武晗鬼公。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized; Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Yuan Duan argued, "According to the posthumous canon, rigid and upright in principle is called Martial; one who relies on power and acts wantonly is called Violent-Brutal—the posthumous name should be Duke Martial Violent-Brutal.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus memorialized; Vice Director Yuan Duan argued, "By the posthumous canon, rigid uprightness is Martial; bullying power is Violent—the name should be Martial Violent Duke.

sentences.zh: 」太常卿元修義議：「忠盡心奉上，翦除凶逆。

translations.literal: Director Yuan Xiuyi argued, "Zhong gave his heart to serve above and cut down fierce rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Director Yuan Xiuyi argued, "Zhong served with all his heart and cut down traitors.

sentences.zh: 依諡法，除偽甯直曰武，夙夜恭事曰敬，宜諡武敬公。

translations.literal: By the posthumous canon, removing falsehood and settling the straight is Martial; diligent service night and day is Reverent—the posthumous name should be Duke Martial Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: By canon, rooting out falsehood is Martial; tireless service is Reverent—the name should be Martial Reverent Duke.

sentences.zh: 」二卿不同。

translations.literal: The two directors differed.
translations.idiomatic: The two directors disagreed.

sentences.zh: 靈太后令依正卿議。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered that the senior director's argument be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager followed the senior director.

sentences.zh: 忠性多阻忌，不交勝己，唯與直閣將軍章初環、千牛備身楊保元為斷金之交。

translations.literal: Zhong by nature was much obstructive and jealous, did not associate with those who surpassed him, and only with Direct Attendant Zhang Chuhuan and Thousand-Ox Guard Yang Baoyuan had bonds like severed metal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was jealous and would not befriend his betters; only Direct Attendant Zhang Chuhuan and Thousand-Ox Guard Yang Baoyuan were his sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 李世哲求寵於忠，私以金帛貨初環、保元，二人談之，遂被賞愛，引為腹心。

translations.literal: Li Shizhe sought favor from Zhong and privately used gold and silk to buy Chuhuan and Baoyuan; the two spoke for him and he was thereupon favored and drawn into the inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhe courted Zhong, bribing Chuhuan and Baoyuan with gold and silk; they spoke for him and he became Zhong's confidant.

sentences.zh: 忠擅權昧進為崇訓之由，皆世哲計也。

translations.literal: Zhong's monopolizing power and blind advancement in Chongxun—all were Shizhe's schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's seizure of power and blind promotions at Chongxun were Shizhe's doing.

sentences.zh: 忠弟景，字百年。

translations.literal: Zhong's younger brother Jing, original name Bainian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's younger brother Jing had originally been named Bainian.

sentences.zh: 忠薨後，為武衛將軍。

translations.literal: After Zhong died he became Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong's death he became Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 謀廢元叉，叉黜為懷荒鎮將。

translations.literal: He plotted to depose Yuan Cha; Cha demoted him to Garrison Commander of Huaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to depose Yuan Cha; Cha sent him to Garrison Commander of Huaihuang.

sentences.zh: 及蠕蠕主阿那瑰叛，鎮人請糧，景不給。

translations.literal: When the Rouran lord Anagui rebelled, the garrison men asked for grain and Jing did not supply it.
translations.idiomatic: When Rouran lord Anagui rebelled, the garrison begged grain; Jing refused.

sentences.zh: 鎮人遂執縛景及其妻，拘守別室，皆去其衣服，令景著皮裘，妻著故絳旗襖，毀辱如此。

translations.literal: The garrison men then seized and bound Jing and his wife, confined them in a separate room, stripped them all of clothing, made Jing wear a fur coat and his wife wear an old crimson banner jacket, and insulted them thus.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison seized Jing and his wife, stripped them, clothed him in furs and her in a tattered crimson banner-coat, and shamed them so.

sentences.zh: 月餘，乃殺之。

translations.literal: After more than a month they killed them.
translations.idiomatic: After a month they killed them both.

sentences.zh: 烈弟果，嚴毅直亮，有父兄風。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Guo was stern, resolute, upright, and bright, with the bearing of father and elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Guo was stern, upright, and bright, in the mold of father and brother.

sentences.zh: 曆朔、華、並、恆四州刺史，賜爵武城子。

translations.literal: He served as Inspector of Shuo, Hua, Bing, and Heng, and was granted Viscount of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He held Shuo, Hua, Bing, and Heng and was made Viscount of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 果弟勁。

translations.literal: Guo's younger brother Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo's younger brother was Jin.

sentences.zh: 勁字鐘葵，頗有武略，位沃野鎮將，賜爵富昌子。

translations.literal: Jin, style name Zhongkui, had considerable military talent; he was Garrison Commander of Woye and granted Viscount of Fuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, styled Zhongkui, was skilled in war; he commanded Woye and was Viscount of Fuchang.

sentences.zh: 宣武納其女為後，封勁太原郡公，妻劉氏為章武郡君。

translations.literal: Xuanwu took his daughter as empress and enfeoffed Jin Duke of Taiyuan; his wife Lady Liu was made Lady of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu made his daughter empress, enfeoffed Jin Duke of Taiyuan, and made his wife Lady Liu Lady of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 後為征北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，諡曰恭莊公。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Duke Gongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously Minister of Works with the posthumous name Duke Gongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 自栗磾至勁，累世貴盛，一皇后，四贈公，三領軍，二尚書令，三開國公。

translations.literal: From Lidi to Jin, for generations they were noble and grand—one empress, four posthumous dukes, three Generals of the Guards, two Directors of the Secretariat, three founding dukes.
translations.idiomatic: From Lidi to Jin the house flourished for generations—one empress, four posthumous dukes, three Guard generals, two Secretariat directors, three founding dukes.

sentences.zh: 勁雖以後父，但以順後早崩，竟不居公輔。

translations.literal: Though Jin was father of the empress, because Empress Shun died early he never reached chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jin was the empress's father, Empress Shun's early death kept him from the highest office.

sentences.zh: 子暉，字宣明，後母弟也。

translations.literal: His son Hui, style name Xuanming, was a son of the later wife.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui, styled Xuanming, was born of the later wife.

sentences.zh: 少有氣幹。

translations.literal: In youth he had spirit and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Young he showed spirit and capacity.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，位汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was Inspector of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the fief and became Inspector of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 暉善事人，為爾硃榮所親，以女妻其子長儒。

translations.literal: Hui was skilled at winning men and was favored by Erzhu Rong, who gave his daughter to Rong's son Changru.
translations.idiomatic: Hui knew how to win hearts; Erzhu Rong favored him and gave him his daughter for son Changru.

sentences.zh: 曆侍中、河南尹。

translations.literal: He served as Palace Attendant and Mayor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Attendant and Mayor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 後兼尚書僕射、東南道行台，與齊神武討平羊侃於兗州。

translations.literal: Later he was concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat and Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit, and with Qi Shenwu subdued Yang Kan in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Vice Director and Southeastern Commissioner and with Qi Shenwu crushed Yang Kan in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，害之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Hui was killed.

sentences.zh: 勁弟天恩，位內行長、遼西太守。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Tian'en was Inner Steward and Governor of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Tian'en was Inner Steward and Governor of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 天恩子仁生，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: Tian'en's son Rensheng was Grand Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Tian'en's son Rensheng was Grand Palace Counselor.

sentences.zh: 仁生子安定，平原郡太守、高平郡都將。

translations.literal: Rensheng's son Anding was Administrator of Pingyuan and Chief Commandant of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Rensheng's son Anding was Administrator of Pingyuan and Chief Commandant of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 安定子子提，隴西郡守、茂平縣伯。

translations.literal: Anding's son Ziti was Governor of Longxi and Baron of Maoping.
translations.idiomatic: Anding's son Ziti was Governor of Longxi and Baron of Maoping.

sentences.zh: 周保定二年，以子謹著勳，追贈太保、建平郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhou's Baoding, because son Jin's merit was illustrious, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Duke of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Baoding year two, for son Jin's merit, Ziti's line was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Duke of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 謹字思敬，小名巨引。

translations.literal: Jin, style name Sijing, childhood name Juyin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, styled Sijing, childhood name Juyin.

sentences.zh: 沈深有識量，略窺經史，尤好《孫子》兵書。

translations.literal: Deep and reserved with discernment, he glanced at classics and histories and especially loved Sunzi's Art of War.
translations.idiomatic: Deep, reserved, and discerning, he skimmed the classics and especially loved Sunzi's Art of War.

sentences.zh: 屏居未有仕進志。

translations.literal: Living in seclusion he had no wish to advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he had no wish for office.

sentences.zh: 或有勸之者，謹曰：「州郡之職，昔人所鄙，台鼎之位，須待時來。

translations.literal: When some urged him, Jin said, "Posts of prefecture and commandery the ancients despised; the tripod of state one must await the right time.
translations.idiomatic: When urged to serve, Jin said, "Prefectures and commanderies ancients scorned; the highest offices wait on the hour.

sentences.zh: 」太宰元天穆見之，歎曰：「王佐材也。

translations.literal: " Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu saw him and sighed, "Material for a king's assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu saw him and sighed, "A king's right hand.

sentences.zh: 」及破六韓拔陵首亂北境，引蠕蠕為授，大行台元纂討之。

translations.literal: " When Poliuhan Baling first raised turmoil on the northern border and drew the Rouran as allies, the Grand Commissioner Yuan Zuan campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Poliuhan Baling first rebelled in the north and called in the Rouran, Commissioner Yuan Zuan marched against him.

sentences.zh: 夙聞謹名，辟為鎧曹參軍事，從軍北伐。

translations.literal: Long having heard Jin's name, he recruited him as Registrar of Armor and he followed the army north.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had long heard of Jin and made him Armor Registrar on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕逃出塞，纂令謹追之，前後十七戰，盡降其眾。

translations.literal: The Rouran fled beyond the passes; Zuan ordered Jin to pursue them—seventeen battles in all—and all their masses surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran fled the border; Zuan sent Jin after them; seventeen battles later all had submitted.

sentences.zh: 後率輕騎出塞覘賊，屬鐵勒數千騎奄至。

translations.literal: Later he led light cavalry beyond the passes to scout the enemy; several thousand Tiele horsemen suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Later he led light horse beyond the passes to scout; thousands of Tiele horsemen fell upon him.

sentences.zh: 謹以眾寡不敵，乃散其騎，使匿叢薄間。

translations.literal: Jin, seeing his force too few to match them, scattered his riders and hid them in thickets.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Jin scattered his riders into the brush.

sentences.zh: 又遣人升山指麾，若分部軍眾。

translations.literal: He also sent men up the mountain to signal as if dividing the army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men up the hills to signal as though deploying divisions.

sentences.zh: 賊望見，雖疑有伏，恃眾不以為慮，乃進逼謹。

translations.literal: The enemy saw it; though they suspected an ambush, trusting their numbers they did not worry and pressed upon Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy saw this; though they feared ambush, their numbers made them bold and they pressed Jin.

sentences.zh: 以常乘駿馬一紫一騧，賊先所識，乃使二人各乘一馬，突陣而出。

translations.literal: His usual mounts were one bay and one piebald the enemy already knew; he therefore had two men each ride one horse and burst through the array.
translations.idiomatic: His usual mounts were a bay and a piebald the enemy knew; he set two men on those horses to break the line.

sentences.zh: 賊以為謹，爭逐之。

translations.literal: The enemy thought it was Jin and strove to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: The foe took them for Jin and gave chase.

sentences.zh: 乃率餘軍擊其追騎。

translations.literal: He then led the remaining troops to strike their pursuing horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then struck the pursuers with his remnant force.

sentences.zh: 賊走，因得入塞。

translations.literal: The enemy fled and he was thus able to enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: They fled and he re-entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 正光四年，行台、廣陽王元深北伐，引謹為長流參軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengguang, Commissioner Prince Yuan Shen of Guangyang marched north; he recruited Jin as Registrar of the Long Stream.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang year four Prince Yuan Shen of Guangyang marched north and took Jin as Long Stream Registrar.

sentences.zh: 特相禮接，使其世子佛陁拜焉。

translations.literal: He treated him with special courtesy and had his heir Fotuo bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen honored him specially and had his heir Fotuo perform obeisance.

sentences.zh: 遂與廣陽破賊主斛律野穀祿等。

translations.literal: He then with Guangyang broke the bandit chief Hulu Yegulu and others.
translations.idiomatic: With Guangyang he broke the bandit chief Hulu Yegulu and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 謹請馳往喻之。

translations.literal: Jin asked to ride ahead and persuade them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin asked to ride ahead and win them by persuasion.

sentences.zh: 謹兼解諸國語，乃單騎入賊，示以恩信，於是西部鐵勒酋長也列河等三萬餘戶並款附，相率南遷。

translations.literal: Jin also understood the languages of many states; he entered the enemy camp alone on one horse, showed grace and trust, and thereupon chieftains of the western Tiele such as Yelie He, more than thirty thousand households, all submitted and came south in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Jin knew many tongues; alone he rode into the enemy camp, showed grace and faith, and western Tiele chiefs including Yelie He—thirty thousand households—submitted and moved south.

sentences.zh: 廣陽與謹至析郭嶺迎接之。

translations.literal: Guangyang with Jin went to Xige Ridge to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyang and Jin met them at Xige Ridge.

sentences.zh: 謹曰：「拔陵兵眾不少，聞也列河等款附，必來要擊。

translations.literal: Jin said, "Baling's troops are not few; hearing that Yelie He and others have submitted, he is sure to come to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "Baling's host is large; hearing of Yelie He's submission, he will intercept.

sentences.zh: 彼若先據險，則難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: If he first holds the defiles, we cannot contend for advantage.
translations.idiomatic: If he seizes the passes first, we cannot fight him on equal ground.

sentences.zh: 今以也烈河等鉺之，當競來抄掠，然後設伏而待，必指掌破之。

translations.literal: Now use Yelie He and the rest as bait—he will surely come to plunder in rivalry; then set an ambush and wait, and you will break him as easily as turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Use Yelie He as bait; Baling will rush to plunder; then ambush him and break him in the palm of your hand.

sentences.zh: 」廣陽然其計。

translations.literal: Guangyang approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyang agreed.

sentences.zh: 拔陵果來要擊，破也列河於嶺上，部眾皆沒。

translations.literal: Baling indeed came to intercept; he broke Yelie He on the ridge and all his following perished.
translations.idiomatic: Baling came to intercept, shattered Yelie He on the ridge, and destroyed his following.

sentences.zh: 謹伏兵發，賊大敗，悉破收也列河之眾。

translations.literal: Jin's ambush troops rose; the bandits were greatly defeated and he gathered and broke all of Yelie He's people.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's ambush rose; the rebels were routed and he recovered Yelie He's people.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年，又隨廣陽王征鮮于修禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang he again followed Prince of Guangyang to campaign against Xianyu Xiuli.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang year one he again followed Guangyang against Xianyu Xiuli.

sentences.zh: 軍次白斗牛邏。

translations.literal: The army halted at White Bull Fighting Camp.
translations.idiomatic: The army camped at White Bull Fighting Camp.

sentences.zh: 會章武王為修禮所害，遂停軍中山。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhangwu was killed by Xiuli, the army stopped at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhangwu fell to Xiuli; the army halted at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 侍中元晏宣言于靈太后曰：「廣陽盤桓不進，坐圖非望。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yuan Yan declared to Empress Dowager Ling, "Guangyang lingers without advancing, sitting and plotting unseemly aims.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Yuan Yan told Empress Dowager Ling, "Guangyang stalls and plots beyond his station.

sentences.zh: 又有于謹者，智略過人，為其謀主，恐非陛下純臣。

translations.literal: Moreover there is Yu Jin, whose stratagems surpass others and who is his chief planner—I fear he is not Your Majesty's pure servant.
translations.idiomatic: His chief planner Yu Jin exceeds ordinary wit—I fear he is no loyal servant of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后詔于尚書省門外立榜，募獲謹者，許以重賞。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager decreed a placard set outside the gate of the Ministry of the Imperial Secretariat offering a heavy reward to whoever captured Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager posted a placard at the Secretariat gate offering a rich reward for Jin's capture.

sentences.zh: 謹聞之，請詣闕披露腹心，廣陽許之。

translations.literal: Jin heard of it and asked to go to the palace and lay bare his heart; Guangyang permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin heard and asked to go to court and lay bare his heart; Guangyang consented.

sentences.zh: 謹遂到榜下，曰：「吾知此人。

translations.literal: Jin then came beneath the placard and said, "I know this man.
translations.idiomatic: Jin came to the placard and said, "I know this man.

sentences.zh: 」眾共詰之，謹曰；

translations.literal: The crowd together questioned him; Jin said:
translations.idiomatic: The crowd pressed him; Jin said:

sentences.zh: 「我即是也。

translations.literal: "I am he.
translations.idiomatic: "I am he.

sentences.zh: 」有司以聞。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The officers reported it.

sentences.zh: 靈後見之，大怒。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager saw him and was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager received him in great anger.

sentences.zh: 謹備述廣陽忠款，兼陳停軍之狀。

translations.literal: Jin fully set forth Guangyang's loyal intent and together stated the reason for halting the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jin laid out Guangyang's loyalty and the army's reasons for halting.

sentences.zh: 靈後遂舍之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then released him.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager spared him.

sentences.zh: 後從爾硃天光與齊神武戰于韓陵山，天光敗，謹遂入關。

translations.literal: Later he followed Erzhu Tian Guang in battle with Qi Shenwu at Hanling Mountain; Tian Guang was defeated and Jin then entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Erzhu Tian Guang against Qi Shenwu at Hanling; Tian Guang lost and Jin entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 周文帝臨夏州，以謹為防城大都督，兼夏州長史。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wendi came to Xiazhou he made Jin Grand Defender of the City and Concurrent Chief Administrator of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Wendi came to Xiazhou he made Jin Grand Defender and Concurrent Administrator.

sentences.zh: 及賀拔岳被害，周文赴平涼。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue was killed, Wendi went to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue was murdered, Wendi went to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 謹言于周文曰：「關中秦漢舊都，古稱天府。

translations.literal: Jin spoke to Wendi, "Guanzhong is the old capital of Qin and Han, anciently called the Storehouse of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jin told Wendi, "Guanzhong was Qin and Han's capital, the ancient Storehouse of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今若據其要害，招集英雄，足觀時變。

translations.literal: If we now hold its strategic points and gather heroes, we may well watch the times change.
translations.idiomatic: Hold its passes and gather heroes and we can read the times.

sentences.zh: 且天子在洛，逼迫群凶。

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven is in Luoyang, pressed by a host of villains.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven sits in Luoyang, harried by villains.

sentences.zh: 請都關右，然後挾天子而令諸侯，千載一時也。

translations.literal: I beg to establish the capital in the west of the passes, then hold the Son of Heaven and command the feudal lords—a chance once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Move the capital west of the passes, hold the Son of Heaven, and command the lords—a chance once in a millennium.

sentences.zh: 」周文大悅。

translations.literal: Wendi was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi was delighted.

sentences.zh: 會有敕追謹為關內大都督，謹因進都關中策。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict recalled Jin as Grand Commander Within the Passes; Jin thereupon advanced the plan to establish the capital in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him as Grand Commander Within the Passes; Jin advanced the Guanzhong capital plan.

sentences.zh: 魏帝西遷，仍從周文征潼關，破回洛城，授北雍州刺史，進爵藍田縣公。

translations.literal: When the Wei Emperor moved west he still followed Wendi in the campaign for Tong Pass, broke Huiluo city, was appointed Inspector of Beiyong, and advanced to Duke of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei Emperor moved west he followed Wendi to Tong Pass, took Huiluo, became Inspector of Beiyong, and was made Duke of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，大軍東伐，為前鋒，進拔弘農，禽東魏陝州刺史李徽伯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, the great army campaigned east; as vanguard he advanced and took Hongnong and captured Eastern Wei Inspector of Shaan Li Huibo.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year three, as eastern vanguard he took Hongnong and captured Eastern Wei Inspector of Shaan Li Huibo.

sentences.zh: 神武至沙苑，謹力戰，進爵常山郡公。

translations.literal: Shenwu came to Shayuan; Jin fought fiercely and was advanced to Duke of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu came to Shayuan; Jin fought hard and was advanced Duke of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 又從戰河橋，拜大丞相府長史，兼大行台尚書。

translations.literal: He again followed in the battle at Heqiao and was appointed Chief Clerk of the Grand Chancellor's Office and Concurrent Director of the Grand Commissioner of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Heqiao and became Chief Clerk to the Grand Chancellor and Concurrent Director of the Grand Commissioner's Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 再遷太子太保。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 芒山之戰，大軍不利，謹率麾下偽降，立于路左。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mang Mountain the main army fared ill; Jin led his subordinates in feigned surrender and stood on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: At Mang Mountain the main force was losing; Jin led his men in a false surrender and posted them on the left side of the road.

sentences.zh: 神武乘勝逐北，不以為虞。

translations.literal: Gao Huan, pressing the victory in pursuit northward, took no precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, riding the victory in pursuit, suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 謹自後擊之，敵人大駭。

translations.literal: Jin struck from the rear; the enemy were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin struck from behind, and the enemy panicked.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信又收兵於後奮擊，神武軍亂，以此大軍得全。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin also gathered troops in the rear and struck fiercely; Gao Huan's army fell into disorder, and by this the main army was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin rallied men behind them and hit hard; Gao Huan's lines broke, and the main army escaped intact.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜尚書左僕射，領司農卿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and concurrently Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he became Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and also Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 及侯景款附，請兵為援，謹諫以為景情難測，周文不聽。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing came over in submission and asked for troops as aid, Jin remonstrated that Jing's intentions could not be gauged; Yuwen Tai would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing submitted and asked for reinforcements, Jin warned that Jing's loyalty was unknowable; Yuwen Tai would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 尋兼大行台尚書、大丞相長史，率兵鎮潼關，加授華州刺史，賜秬鬯一卣，珪瓚副焉。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally Grand Master of Writing on the Great Pacification Commission and Chief Clerk to the Grand Chancellor, leading troops to garrison Tong Pass, further appointed Governor of Hua Province, granted one jar of black-millet ale, with jade libation vessels as the secondary gift.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also Grand Master of Writing on the Great Pacification Commission and chief clerk to the Grand Chancellor, commanding troops at Tong Pass; he was made Governor of Hua, granted a jar of black-millet ale and jade libation vessels besides.

sentences.zh: 俄拜司空。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年，除雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was made Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 初，梁元帝於江陵嗣位，密與齊交通，將謀侵軼。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jiangling succeeded to the throne and secretly communicated with Qi, intending to invade and raid.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne at Jiangling, he had secretly dealt with Qi and planned an incursion.

sentences.zh: 其兄子岳陽王詧時為雍州刺史，以梁元帝殺其兄譽，逐結隙，據襄陽來附。
