translations.literal: His elder brother's son, the Prince of Yueyang Cha, was then Governor of Yong; because Emperor Yuan had killed his elder brother Yu, a breach opened between them, and Cha seized Xiangyang and came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Cha, Prince of Yueyang, held Yong; when Yuan killed Cha's brother Yu, the rift was beyond repair—Cha seized Xiangyang and defected.

sentences.zh: 乃命謹出討。

translations.literal: Jin was then ordered to march out against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was ordered to march against him.

sentences.zh: 周文餞于青泥穀。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai saw him off at Qingni Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai saw him off at Qingni Valley.

sentences.zh: 長孫儉曰：「為蕭繹計將如何？

translations.literal: Changsun Jian said: "What plan will you make for Xiao Yi?"
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Jian asked, "What plan will you make for Xiao Yi?"

sentences.zh: 」謹曰：「曜兵漢沔，席捲度江，直據丹陽，是其上策。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Display troops on the Han and Mian, sweep across and cross the Yangtze, seize Danyang directly—that is the upper stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "Mass troops on the Han and Mian, sweep down the Yangtze, and seize Danyang—that is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 移郭內居人，退保子城，以待援至，是其中策。

translations.literal: Move the people within the outer walls into the inner city and hold the inner city awaiting relief—that is the middle stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Evacuate the outer city into the inner citadel and wait for aid—that is the middling plan."

sentences.zh: 若難於移動，據守羅郭，是其下策。

translations.literal: If moving is difficult and one holds the outer ramparts—that is the lower stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot bear to move and merely holds the outer walls—that is the worst plan."

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「裁繹出何策？

translations.literal: Jian said: "Which stratagem will Yi adopt?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Which will Yi choose?"

sentences.zh: 」謹曰：「必用下。

translations.literal: Jin said: "He will certainly use the lower."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "The worst—certainly."

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「何也？

translations.literal: Jian said: "Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian asked, "Why?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「蕭氏保據江南，綿歷數紀。

translations.literal: He replied: "The House of Xiao has held the south for generations spanning several reigns."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The Xiao have held the south for generations."

sentences.zh: 屬中原有故，未遑外略。

translations.literal: Just when the central plains had troubles, they had no leisure for outward campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: While the central plains were in turmoil they had no leisure to look outward.

sentences.zh: 又以我有齊氏之患，必謂力不能分。

translations.literal: Moreover, because we have the trouble of Qi, he is sure to think our strength cannot be divided.
translations.idiomatic: And seeing our trouble with Qi, he will assume we cannot spare a force.

sentences.zh: 且繹懦而無謀，多疑少斷。

translations.literal: Moreover Yi is timid and without stratagem, suspicious and slow to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yi himself is timid, unstrategic, suspicious, and slow to decide.

sentences.zh: 愚人難與慮始，皆戀邑居，既惡遷移，當保羅郭。

translations.literal: Fools are hard to plan with from the start; all cling to their towns and dwellings, detest removal, and will hold the outer ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Common men hate upheaval; they will cling to their homes, dread moving, and defend the outer walls.

sentences.zh: 所以用下策。

translations.literal: Therefore he will use the lower stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: So he will take the worst plan."

sentences.zh: 」謹令中山公護及大將軍楊忠等先據江津，斷其走路。

translations.literal: Jin ordered the Duke of Zhongshan Hu and the great general Yang Zhong and others first to seize Jiangjin and cut off his escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent the Duke of Zhongshan Hu and the great general Yang Zhong to seize Jiangjin first and cut off retreat.

sentences.zh: 梁人豎木柵於外城，廣輪六十里。

translations.literal: The men of Liang erected wooden palisades on the outer city, sixty li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang raised wooden palisades around the outer city, sixty li around.

sentences.zh: 尋而謹至，悉眾圍之。

translations.literal: Before long Jin arrived and invested it with his full force.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jin arrived and invested the place with his full strength.

sentences.zh: 旬有六日，外城遂陷，梁主退保子城。

translations.literal: After sixteen days the outer city fell; the Liang ruler withdrew to hold the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: In sixteen days the outer city fell; the Liang ruler withdrew into the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 翌日，率其太子以下，面縛出降。

translations.literal: The next day he led his heir apparent and the rest, bound themselves with ropes before Jin, and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he led the crown prince and his court out, bound in ropes, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 尋殺之。

translations.literal: Shortly he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was executed.

sentences.zh: 虜其男女十餘萬人，收其府庫珍寶。

translations.literal: He captured men and women numbering more than a hundred thousand and seized the treasures of the palace storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than a hundred thousand captives and seized the palace treasuries.

sentences.zh: 得宋渾天儀、梁日晷、銅表、魏相風烏、銅蟠螭趺、大玉徑西尺圍七尺及諸輿輦法物以獻，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: They obtained the armillary sphere of Song, the Liang sundial, the bronze gnomon, Wei's wind-indicating bird, the bronze coiled-dragon pedestal, a great jade disk seven feet across and seven feet in circumference, and various chariots and ritual objects, which were presented up; the army took nothing for itself.
translations.idiomatic: They took Song's armillary sphere, the Liang sundial, bronze instruments, Wei's wind-vane bird, a coiled-dragon bronze pedestal, a great jade disk seven feet across, and chariots and ritual gear—all sent up; the army kept nothing private.

sentences.zh: 立蕭詧為梁主，振旅而旋。

translations.literal: Cha was installed as ruler of Liang; the army shook out its banners and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was installed as Liang ruler; the army withdrew in good order.

sentences.zh: 周文親至其第，宴語極歡。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai personally came to his residence; their banquet talk was exceedingly merry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai came in person to his house; their feast ran to great merriment.

sentences.zh: 賞謹奴婢一千口。

translations.literal: Jin was rewarded with a thousand male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was rewarded with a thousand slaves.

sentences.zh: 及梁寶物，並金石絲竹樂一部，別封新野郡公。

translations.literal: Together with Liang treasures, there was also one set of metal, stone, silk, and bamboo music, and he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: With Liang treasures came a full court orchestra; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 謹固辭，不許。

translations.literal: Jin firmly declined; he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin firmly declined; it was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 又令司樂作《常山公平梁歌》十首，使工人歌之。

translations.literal: He also had the Music Office compose ten songs, "The Duke of Changshan Pacifies Liang," and had artisans sing them.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office was ordered to compose ten songs, "The Duke of Changshan Pacifies Liang," for artisans to sing.

sentences.zh: 謹自以久當權重，功名既立，願保優閑，乃上先所乘駿馬及所著鎧甲等。

translations.literal: Jin, considering himself long in heavy authority with merit already established, wished to preserve ease and leisure, and so presented up the fine horses he had formerly ridden and the armor he had worn.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, long in power with his fame made, wished for ease and returned the fine horses and armor he had used.

sentences.zh: 周文識其意，曰：「今巨猾未平，公豈得便爾獨善？

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai understood his intent and said: "The great villain is not yet pacified—how can you alone seek your own good so soon?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai read his intent and said, "The great foe is not yet down—can you seek comfort alone?"

sentences.zh: 」遂不受。

translations.literal: He therefore did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: He would not accept them.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜大司寇。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, Jin was appointed Grand Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he became Grand Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 及周文崩，孝閔帝尚幼，中山公護雖受顧命而名位素下，群公各圖執政。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Tai died, Emperor Xiaomin was still young; the Duke of Zhongshan Hu, though entrusted in the testament, had always ranked below the others, and each duke plotted to seize power.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai died, Emperor Xiaomin was still a child; Hu of Zhongshan, though named in the will, had always ranked low, and every duke plotted for power.

sentences.zh: 護深憂之，密訪於謹。

translations.literal: Hu was deeply worried and secretly consulted Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was deeply worried and sought Jin in secret.

sentences.zh: 謹曰：「夙蒙丞相殊眷，今日必以死爭之。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Having long received the Chancellor's special favor, today I will dispute it to the death."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "I have long owed the Chancellor; today I will dispute this to the death."

sentences.zh: 若對眾定策，公必不得讓。

translations.literal: "If the policy is settled before the assembly, you certainly cannot yield."
translations.idiomatic: "Settle it before the assembly, and you cannot be refused."

sentences.zh: 」明日，群公會議。

translations.literal: The next day the dukes met in council.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the dukes met.

sentences.zh: 謹曰：「昔帝室傾危，丞相志存匡救。

translations.literal: Jin said: "In former days the imperial house was tottering; the Chancellor's will was to rescue and restore."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "When the house was falling, the Chancellor meant to set it right."

sentences.zh: 今上天降禍，奄棄百寮。

translations.literal: "Now Heaven sends calamity and suddenly abandons the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven has sent calamity and taken him from the hundred officials."

sentences.zh: 嗣子雖幼，而中山公親則猶子，兼受顧托，軍國大事，理須歸之。

translations.literal: "The heir, though young, is yet the Duke of Zhongshan, close kin like a son, and also entrusted in the testament—military and state affairs ought by right to fall to him."
translations.idiomatic: "The heir is young, but Hu of Zhongshan is kin like a son and named in the will—state and army belong to him."

sentences.zh: 」辭色抗厲，眾皆悚動。

translations.literal: His words were stern and forceful; all were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: His tone was fierce; everyone flinched.

sentences.zh: 護曰：「此是家事，護何敢有辭！

translations.literal: Hu said: "This is a family matter—how dare Hu decline!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "This is family business—how dare I refuse!"

sentences.zh: 」謹既周文等夷，護每申禮敬。

translations.literal: Jin having been treated as an equal by Yuwen Tai and the rest, Hu always showed him ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had stood as Yuwen Tai's equal; Hu always treated him with ceremony.

sentences.zh: 至是，謹乃起而言曰：「公若統理軍國，謹等便有所依。

translations.literal: At this Jin rose and said: "If you take charge of army and state, we shall have someone to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: Now Jin rose and said, "Take army and state, and we have someone to follow."

sentences.zh: 」遂再拜。

translations.literal: He then bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 群公迫於謹，亦拜。

translations.literal: The dukes, pressed by Jin, also bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by Jin, the dukes bowed as well.

sentences.zh: 眾議始定。

translations.literal: The assembly's decision was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐阼，進封燕國公，邑萬戶，遷太傅、太宗伯，與李弼、侯莫陳崇等參議朝政。

translations.literal: When Xiaomin ascended the throne, Jin was advanced to Duke of Yan with a fief of ten thousand households, transferred to Grand Tutor and Grand Director of the Ancestral Temple, and with Li Bi and Hou Mo Chen Chong and others deliberated on court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaomin took the throne, Jin was made Duke of Yan, fief of ten thousand households, Grand Tutor and Grand Director of the Ancestral Temple, and deliberated policy with Li Bi and Hou Mo Chen Chong.

sentences.zh: 及賀蘭祥討吐谷渾，明帝令謹遙統其軍，授以方略。

translations.literal: When Helan Xiang campaigned against Tuyuhun, Emperor Ming ordered Jin to command his army from afar and gave him strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Helan Xiang marched on Tuyuhun, Emperor Ming had Jin direct the army from afar and gave him the strategy.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，謹以年老，乞骸骨，優詔不許。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, Jin because of age asked to retire; an excellent edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year two, Jin asked to retire on account of age; a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 三年，以謹為三老，固辭，又不許。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made one of the Three Elders; he firmly declined and was again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was made one of the Three Elders; he declined again and was refused again.

sentences.zh: 賜延年杖。

translations.literal: He was granted the staff of longevity.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the staff of longevity.

sentences.zh: 武帝幸太學以食之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu visited the Imperial Academy to feed him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu came to the Imperial Academy to serve him.

sentences.zh: 三老入門，皇帝迎拜屏間，三老答拜。

translations.literal: When the Three Elders entered the gate, the emperor met and bowed to him beyond the screen; the Three Elders returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: As the Three Elders entered, the emperor met and bowed beyond the screen; the Elder bowed in return.

sentences.zh: 有司設三老席於中楹，南向。

translations.literal: The officials set the Three Elders' mat at the central pillar, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Officials set the Elder's mat at the central pillar, facing south.

sentences.zh: 太師、晉公護升階，設席施幾。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor, Duke of Jin Hu, ascended the steps, set the mat and placed the armrest.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, Duke of Jin Hu, mounted the steps and set mat and armrest.

sentences.zh: 三老升席，南面馮幾而坐，師道自居。

translations.literal: The Three Elders ascended the mat, sat facing south leaning on the armrest, placing himself in the teacher's position.
translations.idiomatic: The Elder took the mat, faced south, leaned on the armrest, and held the teacher's place.

sentences.zh: 大司冠、楚國公寧升階，正舄。

translations.literal: The Grand Minister of Justice, Duke of Chu Ning, ascended the steps and straightened his shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Minister of Justice, Duke of Chu Ning, mounted the steps and straightened his shoes.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升，立於斧扆之前，西面。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended and stood before the axe-screen, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted and stood before the axe-screen, facing west.

sentences.zh: 有司進饌，皇帝跪設醬豆，親自袒割。

translations.literal: The officials brought food; the emperor knelt to set out sauce and beans and personally bared his arm to cut the meat.
translations.idiomatic: Food was brought; the emperor knelt to set sauce and beans and cut the meat himself.

sentences.zh: 三老食訖。

translations.literal: When the Three Elders had finished eating,
translations.idiomatic: When the Elder had finished eating,

sentences.zh: 皇帝又親跪授爵以酳。

translations.literal: the emperor again knelt in person to present the cup for rinsing the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor knelt again and offered the rinsing cup.

sentences.zh: 有司撤訖。

translations.literal: The officials withdrew the vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The vessels were cleared away.

sentences.zh: 皇帝北面立訪道。

translations.literal: The emperor stood facing north to inquire about the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stood facing north to ask about the Way.

sentences.zh: 三老乃起立于席。

translations.literal: The Three Elders then rose and stood at the mat.
translations.idiomatic: The Elder rose and stood at his mat.

sentences.zh: 皇帝曰：「猥當天下重任，自惟不才，不知政術之要，公其誨之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I rashly bear the realm's heavy burden; considering myself without talent, I do not know the essentials of governance—please instruct me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I bear the realm's weight unworthily and do not know governance—teach me."

sentences.zh: 」三老答曰：「木從繩則正，君從諫則聖。

translations.literal: The Three Elders answered: "Wood follows the line and becomes straight; a lord who follows remonstrance becomes sage."
translations.idiomatic: The Elder answered, "Wood follows the line and grows straight; a ruler who hears remonstrance becomes sage."

sentences.zh: 自古明王聖主，皆虛心納諫，以知得失，天下乃安。

translations.literal: "From antiquity enlightened kings and sage lords have all received remonstrance with an open mind to know gain and loss, and the realm was thereby secure."
translations.idiomatic: "Sage kings of old all welcomed honest counsel to know their errors, and the realm was secure."

sentences.zh: 惟陛下念之。

translations.literal: "May Your Majesty keep this in mind."
translations.idiomatic: "May Your Majesty remember this."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「為國之本，在乎忠信。

translations.literal: He also said: "The root of governing a state lies in loyalty and trust."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The root of statecraft is loyalty and trust."

sentences.zh: 古人去食去兵，信不可失。

translations.literal: "The ancients would give up food or arms, but trust could not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: "The ancients would give up food or arms, but never trust."

sentences.zh: 國家興廢，莫不由之，願陛下守而勿失。

translations.literal: "The rise and fall of states have never been without this—may Your Majesty hold to it and not lose it."
translations.idiomatic: "States rise and fall by this—hold it and do not let it go."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「為國之道，必須有法。

translations.literal: He also said: "The way to govern a state must have law."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "To govern there must be law."

sentences.zh: 法者，國之綱紀，不可不正。

translations.literal: "Law is the state's cord and net and cannot fail to be set right."
translations.idiomatic: "Law is the state's net—it must be straight."

sentences.zh: 所正在於賞罰。

translations.literal: "What must be set right lies in reward and punishment."
translations.idiomatic: "What must be straight is reward and punishment."

sentences.zh: 若有功必賞，有罪必罰，則為善者日益，為惡者日止。

translations.literal: "If there is merit, reward; if there is crime, punish—then those who do good daily increase and those who do evil daily cease."
translations.idiomatic: "Reward merit and punish crime, and good grows while evil stops."

sentences.zh: 若有功不賞，有罪不罰，則天下善惡不分，下人無所措其手足。

translations.literal: "If there is merit and no reward, crime and no punishment, then good and evil in the realm are not distinguished and inferiors have nowhere to place hand or foot."
translations.idiomatic: "Without reward or punishment, good and evil blur and men have nowhere to stand."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「言行者，立身之基，言出行隨，誠願陛下慎之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Words and conduct are the foundation of establishing the person; words go forth and conduct follows—sincerely may Your Majesty be cautious."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Word and deed are a man's foundation—deeds follow words; be cautious, Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」三老言畢，皇帝再拜受之，三老答拜，禮成而出。

translations.literal: When the Three Elders had finished speaking, the emperor bowed twice to receive it; the Three Elders returned the bow; the rites were completed and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Elder had finished, the emperor bowed twice to receive the teaching; the Elder bowed in return; the rites ended and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護東伐，謹時有病。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Jin Hu campaigned eastward, Jin was then ill.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Hu marched east, Jin was ill.

sentences.zh: 護以其宿將舊臣，猶請與同行，詢訪戎略。

translations.literal: Hu, because he was an old general and veteran minister, still asked him to go together and consulted him on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, honoring an old commander, still asked him along and sought his counsel on strategy.

sentences.zh: 軍還，賜鐘磬一部。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted one set of bells and chimes.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was given bells and chimes.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，又賜安車一乘。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he was again granted one cushioned carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year two he was again granted a cushioned carriage.

sentences.zh: 尋授雍州牧。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 三年，薨，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he died, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 武帝親臨。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person.

sentences.zh: 詔譙王儉監護喪事，賜繒千段、粟夢千斛，贈本官，加使持節、太師、雍恆等二十州諸軍事、雍州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Qiao Jian to supervise the funeral rites, granted a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain, posthumously conferred his former offices, further made him Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Grand Preceptor, Commander-in-Chief over twenty provinces including Yong and Heng, Governor of Yong, posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qiao Jian was ordered to oversee the funeral; a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain were granted; his offices were posthumously confirmed, with Bearer of the Staff, Grand Preceptor, command over twenty provinces including Yong and Heng, Governor of Yong, posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 及葬，王公以下，咸送郊外。

translations.literal: At the burial, from princes and dukes downward all escorted him beyond the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial, princes and dukes alike escorted him beyond the city.

sentences.zh: 配享于文帝廟庭。

translations.literal: He received paired sacrifice in the temple hall of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was given paired sacrifice in Emperor Wen's temple.

sentences.zh: 謹有智謀，善於事上。

translations.literal: Jin had stratagems and was skilled at serving superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was resourceful and skilled at serving his superiors.

sentences.zh: 名位雖重，愈存謙挹，每朝參往來，不過從兩三騎而已。

translations.literal: Though his fame and rank were weighty, he became all the more humble; each time he went to court he took no more than two or three mounted followers.
translations.idiomatic: For all his rank he grew more modest; going to court he took only two or three riders.

sentences.zh: 朝廷凡有軍國之務，多與謹決。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had military or state affairs, it mostly decided them with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court faced army or state matters, it mostly settled them with Jin.

sentences.zh: 謹亦竭其智慧，故功臣中特見委信，始終若一，人無間言。

translations.literal: Jin also exhausted his wisdom; therefore among the meritorious he was especially entrusted, from beginning to end as one, and no man spoke against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin gave his wit fully; among the great ministers he alone was trusted start to finish, without a whisper against him.

sentences.zh: 每誡諸子，務存靜退。

translations.literal: He always admonished his sons to keep to quiet withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: He always warned his sons to seek quiet and withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 加以年齒遐長，禮遇隆重，子孫繁衍，皆至顯達，當時莫比。

translations.literal: Moreover his years were very long and his honors heavy; his sons and grandsons multiplied, all reaching high eminence—none in the time compared.
translations.idiomatic: He lived to great age in heavy honor; his descendants multiplied and rose high—none could match it then.

sentences.zh: 子寔嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 寔字賓實，少和厚，以軍功封萬年縣子。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Bingshi, was from youth gentle and generous; for military merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Bingshi, was gentle from youth; for military merit he was made Viscount of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 大統十四年，累遷尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Datong he was promoted in succession to Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year fourteen he rose to Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 是歲，周文帝與魏太子西巡，寔時從行。

translations.literal: That year Zhou Emperor Wen and the Wei heir apparent toured west; Shi then followed on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yuwen Tai and the Wei crown prince toured west; Shi went with them.

sentences.zh: 周文刻石隴山上，錄功臣名位，以次鐫勒，預以寔為開府儀同三司，至十五年方授之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai carved stone on Long Mountain, recording the meritorious by name and rank in order and carving them; Shi was beforehand named Opening the Government with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and only in the fifteenth year was the appointment conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai carved the meritorious on Long Mountain in order of rank; Shi was named in advance to Opening the Government with Three Excellencies' standing, but received it only in year fifteen.

sentences.zh: 尋除渭州刺史，特給鼓吹一部，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made Governor of Wei Prefecture, specially granted one set of drums and pipes, and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Governor of Wei, granted drums and pipes, and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，羌東令姐率部落反，西連吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, the Qiang chieftain Donglingjie led his tribes in revolt, linking west with Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gong's second year the Qiang chieftain Donglingjie rebelled, allying west with Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 大將軍豆盧甯討之，逾時不克。

translations.literal: The great general Doulu Ning campaigned against him but for a long time could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The great general Doulu Ning campaigned but could not break him.

sentences.zh: 又令寔往，遂破之。

translations.literal: Shi was again sent; he then defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was sent again and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 周文手書勞問，賜奴婢一百口，馬百匹。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai wrote in his own hand to comfort and inquire, granting a hundred male and female slaves and a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai wrote in his own hand to praise him, granting a hundred slaves and a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，授戶部中大夫，進爵延壽郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed Chief of the Households Bureau and advanced in fief to Duke of Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaomin took the throne, he became Chief of the Households Bureau and Duke of Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，延州蒲川賊郝三郎反，攻丹州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, the Pu River bandits of Yan Province, the outlaw Hao Sanlang, rebelled and attacked Dan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year two, Hao Sanlang of Yan's Pu River rebelled and attacked Dan.

sentences.zh: 遣寔討平之，仍除延州刺史。

translations.literal: Shi was sent to pacify them and was then made Governor of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was sent to crush them and was made Governor of Yan.

sentences.zh: 五年，襲燕國公，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he inherited the ducal title of Yan and was advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he inherited the dukedom of Yan and became Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 以罪免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 尋復本官，除涼州總管。

translations.literal: Shortly his former office was restored and he was made Commander-in-Chief of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his office was restored and he was made Commander-in-Chief of Liang.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，加上柱國，拜大左輔。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang he was further made Supreme Pillar of State and appointed Grand Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: In Daxiang year two he was made Supreme Pillar of State and Grand Left Assistant.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年，薨，贈司空，諡曰安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sui's founding he died; posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui's founding year he died, posthumously Minister of Works, titled An.

sentences.zh: 子顗。

translations.literal: His son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan.

sentences.zh: 顗字元武，身長八尺，美鬚眉。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Yuanwu, was eight feet tall with fine beard and brows.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Yuanwu, stood eight feet with handsome beard and brows.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護見而器之，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Zhou's Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu saw him and valued him, giving him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, Zhou's Grand Chancellor, favored him and gave him his daughter.

sentences.zh: 以父勳，賜爵新野郡公。

translations.literal: Because of his father's merit he was granted the fief of Duke of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: For his father's merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 曆左右宮伯、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Left and Right Palace Defender and Governor of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left and Right Palace Defender and Governor of Ying in turn.

sentences.zh: 大象中，以水軍總管從韋孝寬經略淮南。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era, as Commander of the Water Army he followed Wei Xiaokuan in planning for Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daxiang he commanded the water army under Wei Xiaokuan in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥之反，時總管趙文表與顗素不協，顗將圖之，因臥閣內，詐疾。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, the commander Zhao Wenbiao and Yan had long been at odds; Yan intended to deal with him and therefore lay in his pavilion feigning illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Commander Zhao Wenbiao was Yan's enemy; Yan feigned illness in his pavilion to trap him.

sentences.zh: 文表獨至，顗殺之。

translations.literal: Wenbiao came alone; Yan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao came alone; Yan killed him.

sentences.zh: 因言文表與迥通謀，其麾下無敢動者。

translations.literal: He then said Wenbiao had conspired with Jiong; his subordinates dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Wenbiao had conspired with Jiong; his troops dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 時隋文帝以迥未平，慮顗復生邊患，因宥免之，即拜吳州總管。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wen of Sui, because Jiong was not yet pacified, feared Yan would again raise border trouble and therefore pardoned and released him, at once appointing him Commander of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, Jiong not yet down, feared Yan would stir the frontier and pardoned him, making him Commander of Wu at once.

sentences.zh: 以頻敗陳師，賜采數百段。

translations.literal: For repeatedly defeating Chen armies he was granted several hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated victories over Chen he was granted hundreds of bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 及隋受禪，文表弟詣闕稱兄無罪。

translations.literal: When Sui received the abdication, Wenbiao's younger brother came to court saying his brother was innocent.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui took the throne, Wenbiao's brother came to court pleading his innocence.

sentences.zh: 上令按其事，太傅竇熾等議顗當死。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the matter investigated; the Grand Tutor Dou Chi and others judged Yan should die.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry; Grand Tutor Dou Chi and others ruled Yan should die.

sentences.zh: 上以其門著勳績，特原之，貶為開府。

translations.literal: The emperor, because his house had outstanding merit, especially pardoned him and demoted him to Opening the Government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, honoring the family's merit, pardoned him specially and demoted him to Opening the Government.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵燕國公。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited the dukedom of Yan.

sentences.zh: 尋拜澤州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Governor of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Governor of Ze.

sentences.zh: 免，卒於家。

translations.literal: Dismissed, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 子世虔。

translations.literal: His son Shiqian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiqian.

sentences.zh: 顗弟仲文。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 仲文字次武，少聰敏，髫齔就學，耽習不倦。

translations.literal: Zhongwen, styled Ciwu, was from youth clever and keen; while still in childhood he went to study and was absorbed in learning without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen, styled Ciwu, was clever as a boy; he studied without tiring even in childhood.

sentences.zh: 父寔異之，曰：「此兒必興吾宗。

translations.literal: His father Shi marveled at him and said: "This boy will surely raise our clan."
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi said in wonder, "This boy will raise our house."

sentences.zh: 」九歲，嘗于雲陽宮見周文帝。

translations.literal: At nine he once met Zhou Emperor Wen at Yunyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he met Yuwen Tai at Yunyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 問曰：「聞兒好讀書，書有何事？

translations.literal: He asked: "I hear the boy loves reading—what business has reading?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai asked, "I hear you love books—what is reading for?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「資父事君，忠孝而已。

translations.literal: He replied: "To support one's father and serve one's lord—loyalty and filial piety, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "To support one's father and serve one's lord—loyalty and filial piety, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 」周文甚嗟歎之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai greatly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sighed in deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 後就博士李詳受《周易》、《三禮》，略通大義。

translations.literal: Later he studied under the Erudite Li Xiang and received the Book of Changes and the Three Rites, grasping the great principles in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied the Changes and the Three Rites under Erudite Li Xiang and grasped their main points.

sentences.zh: 及長，倜儻有大志，氣調英拔。

translations.literal: When grown he was free and easy with great ambition, his spirit and tone outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was bold and ambitious, his bearing striking.

sentences.zh: 起家為趙王屬，安固太守。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant to the Prince of Zhao and Governor of Angu.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Attendant to the Prince of Zhao and Governor of Angu.

sentences.zh: 有任、杜兩家各失牛，後得一牛，兩家俱認，州郡久不決。

translations.literal: The Ren and Du families each lost an ox; later one ox was found and both families claimed it; the prefecture and district long could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Ren and Du families each lost an ox; when one was found both claimed it, and the prefecture could not decide.

sentences.zh: 益州長史韓伯俊曰：「于安固少年聰察，可令決之。

translations.literal: Han Bojun, chief clerk of Yi Province, said: "The youth of Angu is clever and perceptive—he can be ordered to decide it."
translations.idiomatic: Yi Province chief clerk Han Bojun said, "The young man of Angu is sharp—let him decide."

sentences.zh: 」仲文曰：「此易解耳。

translations.literal: Zhongwen said: "This is easy to resolve."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen said, "That is easily settled."

sentences.zh: 」乃令二家各驅牛群至，乃放所認者，牛遂向任氏群中。

translations.literal: He then ordered the two families each to drive their herds of oxen forward and released the disputed ox; the ox at once went toward the Ren family's herd.
translations.idiomatic: He had both herds driven up and turned the disputed ox loose; it walked straight to Ren's herd.

sentences.zh: 又使人微傷其牛，任氏嗟惋，杜氏自若。

translations.literal: He also had men slightly wound the ox; the Ren family lamented, the Du family were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He had the ox lightly hurt; Ren's people wailed, Du's were unmoved.

sentences.zh: 仲文遂訶詰杜氏，服罪而去。

translations.literal: Zhongwen then sternly questioned the Du family; they confessed guilt and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen pressed the Du family; they confessed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 始州刺史屈突尚，宇文護之黨也。

translations.literal: Qu Tu Shang, Governor of Shizhou, was a partisan of Yuwen Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tu Shang of Shizhou was Yuwen Hu's man.

sentences.zh: 先坐事下獄，無敢繩者。

translations.literal: He had earlier been imprisoned for an offense; none dared prosecute him.
translations.idiomatic: He had been jailed for a crime; none dared touch him.

sentences.zh: 仲文至郡，窮之，遂竟其獄。

translations.literal: When Zhongwen reached the commandery he investigated to the end and completed the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongwen took the commandery he investigated to the end and closed the case.

sentences.zh: 蜀中語曰：「明斷無雙有於公，不避強禦有次武。

translations.literal: In Shu they said: "For clear judgment without peer there is Duke Yu; for not shunning the powerful there is Ciwu."
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "Clear judgment without peer—Duke Yu; fearing no power—Ciwu."

sentences.zh: 」徵為禦正下大夫，封延壽郡公，以勳授儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Junior Master of Rectitude, enfeoffed Duke of Yanshou, and for merit granted ceremonial rank equal to Opening the Government.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Junior Master of Rectitude, made Duke of Yanshou, and for merit given Opening the Government's ceremonial rank.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，為東郡太守。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan he was Governor of Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he was Governor of Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥作亂，使誘仲文，仲文拒之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong raised rebellion he sent to entice Zhongwen; Zhongwen refused him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong rebelled he tried to win Zhongwen; Zhongwen refused.

sentences.zh: 迥遣儀同宇文威攻之。

translations.literal: Jiong sent the ceremonial peer Yuwen Wei to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent Yuwen Wei to attack him.

sentences.zh: 仲文迎擊，大破威，以功授開府。

translations.literal: Zhongwen met the attack and greatly defeated Wei; for the merit he was appointed Opening the Government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen met him and routed him; for the merit he was made Opening the Government.

sentences.zh: 迥又遣其將宇文胄度石濟。

translations.literal: Jiong again sent his general Yuwen Zhou to cross the Stone Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong again sent Yuwen Zhou across the Stone Ford.

sentences.zh: 宇文威、鄒紹自白馬，二道俱進，復攻仲文。

translations.literal: Yuwen Wei and Zou Shao from Baima—the two routes advanced together and again attacked Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Wei and Zou Shao came from Baima; two columns struck again.

sentences.zh: 郡人赫連僧伽、敬子哲率眾應迥。

translations.literal: The commandery men Helian Sengqie and Jing Zizhe led the masses to respond to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Sengqie and Jing Zizhe of the commandery rallied men to Jiong.

sentences.zh: 仲文自度不能支，棄妻子，潰圍而遁，達于京師。

translations.literal: Zhongwen judged himself unable to hold; he abandoned wife and children, broke the encirclement and fled, reaching the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not hold, he left wife and children, broke out, and reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 迥屠其三子一女。

translations.literal: Jiong slaughtered his three sons and one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong killed his three sons and one daughter.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝引入臥內，為之下泣，賜采五百段，黃金二百兩。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui led him into the inner chamber and wept for him, granting five hundred bolts of colored silk and two hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen brought him to the inner chamber and wept, granting five hundred bolts of silk and two hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍，領河南道行軍總管，給鼓吹。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Great General and made Commander-in-Chief on the Henan Circuit, granted drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Great General and Commander-in-Chief on the Henan circuit, with drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 馳傳詣洛陽發兵，討迥將檀讓。

translations.literal: He rode post-horses to Luoyang to raise troops and campaign against Jiong's general Tan Rang.
translations.idiomatic: He raced to Luoyang to raise troops against Jiong's general Tan Rang.

sentences.zh: 時韋孝寬拒迥於永橋。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Xiaokuan held Jiong at Yong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan then held Jiong at Yong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 仲文詣之，有所計議。

translations.literal: Zhongwen went to him and they deliberated plans.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen went to him to plan.

sentences.zh: 總管宇文忻頗有自疑心，因謂仲文曰：「尉遲迥誠不足平，正恐事寧後，更有藏弓之慮。

translations.literal: The commander Yuwen Xin was rather suspicious on his own account and therefore said to Zhongwen: "Yuchi Jiong is truly not hard to pacify; I only fear that after matters settle there will again be the worry of 'the bow hidden when the birds are gone.'"
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yuwen Xin was suspicious and said to Zhongwen, "Jiong is easy—but when birds are gone, bows are stored away. I fear that after victory."

sentences.zh: 」仲文懼忻生變，謂曰：「丞相寬仁大度，明識有餘，仲文在京三日，頻見三善，非常人也。

translations.literal: Zhongwen feared Xin would change; he said to him: "The Chancellor is generous and magnanimous, clear-sighted and ample; in three days in the capital I frequently saw three goods—he is no ordinary man."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Xin would turn, Zhongwen said, "The Chancellor is generous and far-sighted; in three days in the capital I saw three virtues—no ordinary man."

sentences.zh: 」忻曰：「三善何如？

translations.literal: Xin said: "What are the three goods like?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin asked, "What three?"

sentences.zh: 」仲文曰：「有陳萬敵新從賊中來，丞相即令其弟難敵召募鄉曲，從軍討賊。

translations.literal: Zhongwen said: "There was Chen Wandi newly come from the rebels; the Chancellor at once had his younger brother Nandi recruit village men to follow the army in suppressing bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen said, "Chen Wandi had just defected; the Chancellor had his brother Nandi raise village men to fight bandits."

sentences.zh: 此大度一也。

translations.literal: That is the first magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: That is magnanimity—the first.

sentences.zh: 上士宋謙奉使勾檢，謙緣此別求他罪。

translations.literal: Superior Gentleman Song Qian was sent on a mission to investigate; Qian used this to seek other crimes on the side.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qian was sent to investigate; he used it to hunt other crimes.

sentences.zh: 丞相責之曰：'入綱者自可推求，何須別訪，以虧大體。

translations.literal: The Chancellor reproved him saying: 'Those caught in the net can be pursued within it—why must you inquire separately and harm the great principle.'
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor rebuked him: 'Those in the net can be pursued—why hunt elsewhere and harm the whole?'

sentences.zh: '此不求人私二也。

translations.literal: That is the second—not seeking private advantage from men.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second—not fishing for private gain.

sentences.zh: 言及仲文妻子，未嘗不潸泫。

translations.literal: When he spoke of Zhongwen's wife and children he never failed to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of Zhongwen's wife and children he never failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 此有仁心三也。

translations.literal: That is the third—having a benevolent heart.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third—a benevolent heart.

sentences.zh: 」忻自是遂安。

translations.literal: Xin from this was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was reassured.

sentences.zh: 仲文軍至汴州東，頻破迥將。

translations.literal: Zhongwen's army reached east of Bian Province and repeatedly defeated Jiong's generals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen's army reached east of Bian and repeatedly beat Jiong's generals.

sentences.zh: 進攻梁郡，迥守將劉孝寬棄城走。

translations.literal: He attacked Liang Commandery; Jiong's defending general Liu Xiaokuan abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Liang; Liu Xiaokuan abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 初，仲文在蓼堤，諸將皆曰：「軍自遠來，疲弊不可決戰。

translations.literal: At first, at Liaodi, the generals all said: "The army has come from afar, weary and spent—it cannot give battle."
translations.idiomatic: At Liaodi the generals said, "We are far from home and spent—we cannot fight."

sentences.zh: 」仲文令趣食列陳，既而破賊。

translations.literal: Zhongwen ordered them to take food quickly and form ranks; before long they defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen ordered a quick meal and battle lines; soon the enemy was broken.

sentences.zh: 諸將問其故，笑曰：「吾所部將士皆山東人，果於速進，不宜持久。

translations.literal: The generals asked the reason; he smiled and said: "The officers and men under my command are all men of Shandong, bold in swift advance—not fit for a long stand."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he smiled, "My men are Shandongers—swift attack, not a long fight."

sentences.zh: 乘勢擊之，所以制勝。

translations.literal: "Striking them while the momentum held—that is why we won."
translations.idiomatic: "Strike while hot—that is how we win."

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰：「非所及也。

translations.literal: The generals all said: "Not what we could reach."
translations.idiomatic: The generals said, "Beyond us."

sentences.zh: 」進擊曹州，獲迥所署刺史李仲康及上儀同房勁。

translations.literal: He pressed the attack on Cao Province, capturing Jiong's appointed Governor Li Zhongkang and the ceremonial peer Fang Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Cao, taking Jiong's governor Li Zhongkang and the ceremonial peer Fang Jin.

sentences.zh: 檀讓以余眾屯成武，謂仲文未能卒至，方椎牛饗士。

translations.literal: Tan Rang with the remaining troops camped at Chengwu, thinking Zhongwen could not arrive suddenly, and was just beating oxen to feast the officers.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Rang camped at Chengwu with the remnant, sure Zhongwen could not come at once, feasting his men.

sentences.zh: 仲文選騎襲之，遂拔成武。

translations.literal: Zhongwen chose cavalry to strike him and then took Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen chose cavalry, struck, and took Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 迥將席毗羅，眾十萬，屯沛縣，將攻徐州。

translations.literal: Jiong's general Xi Piluo, with a host of a hundred thousand, camped at Pei County intending to attack Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's general Xi Piluo camped at Pei with a hundred thousand men, set to strike Xu.

sentences.zh: 其妻子在金鄉。

translations.literal: His wife and children were at Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His family was at Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 仲文遣人詐作毗羅使，謂金鄉城主徐善淨曰：檀讓明日午時到金鄉，將宣蜀公令，賞將士。

translations.literal: Zhongwen sent a man falsely posing as Piluo's envoy to say to Xu Shanjing, lord of Jinxiang: "Tan Rang will reach Jinxiang tomorrow at noon to proclaim the Duke of Shu's order and reward the officers."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen sent a false envoy to Jinxiang's lord Xu Shanjing: "Tan Rang arrives tomorrow at noon to proclaim the Duke of Shu's order and reward the troops."

sentences.zh: 」金鄉人謂為信然，皆喜。

translations.literal: The people of Jinxiang thought it true and were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxiang believed it and rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 仲文簡精兵，偽建迥旗幟。

translations.literal: Zhongwen picked elite troops and falsely raised Jiong's banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen picked elite troops and flew Jiong's banners falsely.

sentences.zh: 善淨以為檀讓至，出城迎謁。

translations.literal: Shanjing thought Tan Rang had arrived and went out of the city to meet and pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Shanjing thought Tan Rang had come and went out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 仲文執之，遂取金鄉。

translations.literal: Zhongwen seized him and then took Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen seized him and took Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 諸將勸屠之，仲文曰：「當寬其妻子，其兵可自歸。

translations.literal: The generals urged slaughter; Zhongwen said: "We should treat their wives and children leniently and their soldiers will return of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged massacre; Zhongwen said, "Spare their families and the soldiers will come over."

sentences.zh: 如即屠之，彼皆絕矣。

translations.literal: "If we slaughter at once, they will all be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: "Slaughter them now and every man will fight to the death."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆稱善。

translations.literal: The masses all praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: All approved.

sentences.zh: 於是毗羅恃眾來薄官軍，仲文背城結陣，設伏，兵發，俱拽柴鼓譟。

translations.literal: Thereupon Piluo, relying on his numbers, came to press the government army; Zhongwen with his back to the city formed ranks and set ambush; when the troops moved, all together pulled brushwood drums and raised a clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Piluo, trusting his numbers, pressed the government army; Zhongwen formed with his back to the wall, set ambush, and at the signal every man dragged brushwood drums and roared.

sentences.zh: 毗羅軍潰，皆投洙水死，水為不流。

translations.literal: Piluo's army collapsed; all threw themselves into the Zhu River and died, and the water did not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Piluo's army broke; men threw themselves into the Zhu until the river would not flow.

sentences.zh: 獲檀讓，檻送京師，河南悉平。

translations.literal: Tan Rang was captured and sent to the capital in a caged cart; Henan was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Rang was taken in a cage cart to the capital; Henan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 毗羅匿榮陽人家，執斬之，傳首闕下。

translations.literal: Piluo hid in a house in Xingyang; seized and beheaded, his head was sent to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Piluo hid in Xingyang; seized and beheaded, his head was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 勒石紀功，樹於泗上。

translations.literal: A stone was carved to record the merit and set up on the Si.
translations.idiomatic: A stone was carved to record the victory and set up on the Si.

sentences.zh: 入朝京師，文帝引入臥內，宴享極歡。

translations.literal: He entered court at the capital; Emperor Wen led him into the inner chamber and their feast was exceedingly merry.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court; Emperor Wen brought him to the inner chamber and feasted him in great joy.

sentences.zh: 賜雜采千段，妓女十人，拜柱國。

translations.literal: He was granted a thousand bolts of mixed colored silk, ten singing girls, and appointed Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a thousand bolts of silk, ten singing girls, and made Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 屬文帝受禪，不行。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Wen received the abdication and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wen received the abdication and Zhongwen did not attend.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其叔父太尉翼坐事下獄，仲文亦為吏所簿，於獄中上書曰：「曩者尉迥逆亂，所在景從。

translations.literal: Before long his uncle the Grand Commandant Yi was imprisoned for an offense; Zhongwen was also audited by the clerks, and in prison he submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly when Yuchi Jiong rebelled, everywhere men followed the scene."
translations.idiomatic: Soon his uncle Grand Commandant Yi was jailed; Zhongwen was audited too and from prison wrote: "When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, men followed him everywhere."

sentences.zh: 臣任處關河，地居沖要，嘗潆詹枕戈，誓以必死。

translations.literal: "I held a post at the passes and rivers in a place of strategic weight; I once rinsed my girdle and slept with my spear, vowing certain death."
translations.idiomatic: "I held the passes in a vital post, rinsed my belt and slept with my spear, sworn to die."

sentences.zh: 迥時購臣，位大將軍，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: "At the time Jiong offered to buy me with the rank of Great General and a fief of ten thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: "Jiong offered me Great General and ten thousand households."

sentences.zh: 臣不顧妻子，不愛身命。

translations.literal: "I did not regard wife and children and did not cherish my life."
translations.idiomatic: "I gave up wife and children and my own life."

sentences.zh: 冒白刃，潰重圍，三男一女，相繼淪沒。

translations.literal: "I braved bare blades, broke heavy encirclements; three sons and one daughter perished in succession."
translations.idiomatic: "I broke through steel; three sons and a daughter fell one after another."

sentences.zh: 披露肝膽，馳赴闕庭。

translations.literal: "I laid bare liver and gall and raced to the palace gate."
translations.idiomatic: "I laid bare my heart and came to the throne."

sentences.zh: 蒙陛下授臣以高官，委臣以兵革。

translations.literal: "I received from Your Majesty high office and was entrusted with arms."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty gave me high rank and an army."

sentences.zh: 于時河南凶寇，狼顧鴟張。

translations.literal: "At that time Henan's fierce bandits glared like wolves and spread like owls."
translations.idiomatic: "Henan's rebels glared like wolves and spread like kites."

sentences.zh: 臣以羸兵八千，掃除氛祲。

translations.literal: "With eight thousand worn troops I swept away the miasma."
translations.idiomatic: "With eight thousand worn men I swept the miasma away."

sentences.zh: 摧劉寬于梁郡，破檀讓於蓼堤；

translations.literal: "I overthrew Liu Xiaokuan at Liang Commandery and broke Tan Rang at Liaodi;"
translations.idiomatic: "I broke Liu Xiaokuan at Liang and Tan Rang at Liaodi;"

sentences.zh: 平曹州，復東郡，安成武，定永昌；

translations.literal: "pacified Cao, recovered Dong, secured Chengwu, settled Yongchang;"
translations.idiomatic: "pacified Cao, recovered Dong, held Chengwu, settled Yongchang;"

sentences.zh: 解亳州圍，破徐州賊。

translations.literal: "relieved Bozhou's siege and defeated the Xu bandits."
translations.idiomatic: "lifted Bozhou's siege and beat Xu;"

sentences.zh: 席毗羅十萬之眾，一戰土崩。

translations.literal: "Xi Piluo's host of a hundred thousand collapsed in one battle."
translations.idiomatic: "Piluo's hundred thousand fell in one fight."

sentences.zh: 河南蟻聚之徒，應時戡定。

translations.literal: "Henan's swarming rebels were pacified at the proper time."
translations.idiomatic: "Henan's swarms were cut down in season."

sentences.zh: 當群凶問鼎之際，生靈乏主之辰，臣第二叔翼先在幽州，總馭燕、趙。

translations.literal: "When the many villains contended for the tripod and living creatures lacked a master, my second uncle Yi was first at You Province, commanding Yan and Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: "When traitors fought for the realm and the people had no lord, my second uncle Yi held You, commanding Yan and Zhao."

sentences.zh: 南鄰群寇，北掃旄頭，內安外撫，得免罪戾。

translations.literal: "South he neighbored many bandits; north he swept the barbarian banners; within he pacified, without he soothed, and escaped guilt."
translations.idiomatic: "South he faced rebels, north he swept the frontier, within and without he kept the peace and stood clear."

sentences.zh: 臣第五叔智建ＣＭ黑水，與王謙為鄰，式遏蠻陬，鎮綏蜀道。

translations.literal: "My fifth uncle Zhi raised the standard at Heishui, neighbored Wang Qian, checked the barbarian valleys, and pacified the Shu road."
translations.idiomatic: "My fifth uncle Zhi raised the standard at Heishui beside Wang Qian, checked the barbarian passes, and held the Shu road."

sentences.zh: 臣兄顗作牧淮南，坐制勍敵，乘機剿定，傳首京師。

translations.literal: "My elder brother Yan governed Huainan, sat and controlled fierce enemies, seized the moment to pacify them, and sent heads to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: "My brother Yan held Huainan, pinned fierce foes, struck when he could, and sent heads to the capital."

sentences.zh: 王謙竊據二州，叛換三蜀。

translations.literal: "Wang Qian secretly held two provinces and rebelled across the three Shu."
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Qian held two provinces and rebelled across Shu."

sentences.zh: 臣第三叔義受脤廟庭，恭行天罰。

translations.literal: "My third uncle Yi received the war-meat in the temple court and reverently executed Heaven's punishment."
translations.idiomatic: "My third uncle Yi took the temple charge and carried out Heaven's punishment."

sentences.zh: 自外父叔兄弟，皆當文武重寄。

translations.literal: "Besides these, father, uncles, and brothers all bore heavy civil and military trust."
translations.idiomatic: "Beyond them, father, uncles, and brothers all bore heavy trust of court and camp."

sentences.zh: 或銜命危難，或侍衛鉤陣，合門誠款，冀有可明。

translations.literal: "Some received orders in peril; some attended the hook formation as guards—the whole house sincere, hoping there is what can be made clear."
translations.idiomatic: "Some took orders in peril, some guarded the throne—the whole house loyal, and something may yet be shown."

sentences.zh: 伏願垂泣辜之恩，降雲雨之施，則寒灰更然，枯骨還肉。

translations.literal: "I humbly wish you to grant the grace of tears for the guiltless and send down rain and cloud favor, then cold ash will blaze again and withered bone return to flesh."
translations.idiomatic: "Grant tears for the guiltless and rain from heaven, and cold ash will live and dry bone grow flesh again."

sentences.zh: 」上覽表，並翼釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and released both Yi and Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and freed both Yi and Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜行軍元帥，統十二州總管以擊胡。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Campaign Commander-in-Chief, commanding twelve provincial commanders to strike the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he was Campaign Commander-in-Chief over twelve provinces against the Hu.

sentences.zh: 出服遠鎮，遇虜，破之。

translations.literal: He went out to Fuyuan garrison, met the barbarians, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuyuan he met the barbarians and beat them.

sentences.zh: 於是從金河出白道。

translations.literal: Thereupon from the Golden River he went out by White Road.
translations.idiomatic: Then from the Golden River he marched by White Road.

sentences.zh: 遣總管辛明瑾、元滂、賀蘭志、呂楚、段諧等二萬人出盛樂道，趣那頡山。

translations.literal: He sent the commanders Xin Mingjin, Yuan Pang, Helan Zhi, Lü Chu, Duan Xie, and others with twenty thousand men out by the Shengle route toward Napie Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xin Mingjin, Yuan Pang, Helan Zhi, Lü Chu, Duan Xie, and others with twenty thousand by the Shengle road toward Napie Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至護軍州北，與虜遇。

translations.literal: North of Protecting-the-Army Province they met the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: North of Protecting-the-Army they met the enemy.

sentences.zh: 可汗見仲文軍容整肅，不戰而退。

translations.literal: The khan saw Zhongwen's army array neat and stern and withdrew without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The khan saw Zhongwen's ranks trim and stern and withdrew without battle.

sentences.zh: 仲文逾山追之。

translations.literal: Zhongwen crossed the mountains in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen crossed the mountains in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 及還，上以尚書省文簿繁雜，吏多奸詐，令仲文勘錄省中事，所發擿甚多。

translations.literal: On his return, because the documents of the Masters of Writing were complex and clerks were much given to fraud, the emperor ordered Zhongwen to examine and record affairs within the ministry; what he exposed and impeached was very many.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, finding the Masters of Writing's records tangled and clerks corrupt, the emperor had Zhongwen audit the ministry; he exposed many.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其明斷，厚加勞賞。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his clear judgment and richly rewarded and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his clarity and rewarded him richly.

sentences.zh: 上每憂轉運不給，仲文請決渭水，開漕渠。

translations.literal: The emperor often worried that transport could not be supplied; Zhongwen asked to cut the Wei and open a canal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often worried over supply; Zhongwen proposed cutting the Wei and opening a canal.

sentences.zh: 上然之，使仲文總其事。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it and had Zhongwen oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and put Zhongwen in charge.

sentences.zh: 及伐陳之役，拜行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he was appointed Campaign Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen he was Campaign Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 高智慧等作亂江南，仲文復以行軍總管討之。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in Jiangnan, Zhongwen was again Campaign Commander-in-Chief to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui rebelled in the south, Zhongwen again commanded the campaign.

sentences.zh: 時三軍乏食，米粟踴貴，仲文私糶軍糧，坐除名。

translations.literal: At the time the three armies lacked food and rice and grain soared in price; Zhongwen privately sold army grain and was dismissed from his name.
translations.idiomatic: The armies starved and grain soared; Zhongwen sold army grain privately and was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 明年，復官爵，率兵屯馬邑以備胡。

translations.literal: The next year his office and rank were restored and he led troops to garrison Mayi against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Next year his rank was restored and he garrisoned Mayi against the Hu.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣以仲文有將領才，每常屬意，至是奏之，乃令督晉王軍府事。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang, because Zhongwen had talent as a commander, always kept him in mind; at this he memorialized him, and he was then ordered to supervise the Prince of Jin's military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guang valued his generalship and now recommended him; he was ordered to supervise the prince's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後突厥犯塞，晉王為元帥，使仲文將前軍，大破賊而還。

translations.literal: Later when the Turks raided the frontier, the Prince of Jin was supreme commander and sent Zhongwen to lead the vanguard; he greatly defeated the bandits and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks raided the border, Prince Guang was supreme commander and sent Zhongwen with the vanguard; he routed them and returned.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷左翊衙大將軍，參掌文武選事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Zhongwen was transferred to Grand General of the Left Wing Guard and took part in selecting civil and military appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Zhongwen became Grand General of the Left Wing Guard and helped choose civil and military men.

sentences.zh: 從帝討吐谷渾，進位光祿大夫，甚見親重。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor in the campaign against Tuyuhun and was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness, greatly favored and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor against Tuyuhun, was made Grand Master of Splendid Brightness, and was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，仲文率軍指樂浪道。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign Zhongwen led the army on the Lelang route.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong war he led the Lelang column.

sentences.zh: 次烏骨城，仲文簡羸馬驢數千，置於軍後，既而率眾東過。

translations.literal: When they halted at Wugu City, Zhongwen chose several thousand lean horses and donkeys and placed them at the rear of the army; then he led the host eastward past.
translations.idiomatic: At Wugu he placed several thousand lean horses and donkeys at the rear, then marched east.

sentences.zh: 高麗出兵掩襲輜重，仲文回擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Goryeo sent troops to mask and strike the baggage train; Zhongwen turned back and struck, greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo struck the baggage train; he turned and broke them.

sentences.zh: 至鴨綠水，高麗將乙支文德詐降，來入其菅。

translations.literal: When they reached the Yalu, the Goryeo general Yi Zhizhi Wen De feigned surrender and came into his camp.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yalu, Goryeo's Yi Zhizhi Wen De feigned surrender and entered his camp.

sentences.zh: 仲文先奉密旨，若遇高元及文德者，必禽之。

translations.literal: Zhongwen had earlier received a secret order that if he met Gao Yuan and Wen De he must capture them.
translations.idiomatic: He had a secret order to seize Gao Yuan and Wen De if he met them.

sentences.zh: 至是，文德來，仲文將執之。

translations.literal: At this Wen De came; Zhongwen was about to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen De came; Zhongwen was about to seize him.

sentences.zh: 時尚書右丞劉士龍為慰撫使，固止之。

translations.literal: At the time the Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Shilong was comfort-and-soothe commissioner and firmly stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Liu Shilong, the soothe commissioner, firmly stopped him.

sentences.zh: 仲文遂舍文德。

translations.literal: Zhongwen then released Wen De.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen let Wen De go.

sentences.zh: 尋悔，遣人紿文德曰：「更有言議，可復來也。

translations.literal: Shortly he regretted it and sent a man to deceive Wen De saying: "There is further to discuss—you may come again."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he regretted it and sent word: "There is more to discuss—come again."

sentences.zh: 」文德不從，遂濟。

translations.literal: Wen De would not comply and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wen De refused and crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 仲文選騎度水追之，每戰破賊。

translations.literal: Zhongwen chose cavalry to cross the water in pursuit; in each battle he defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen crossed with cavalry and beat them in every fight.

sentences.zh: 文德遺仲文詩曰：「神策究天文，妙算窮地理。

translations.literal: Wen De sent Zhongwen a poem saying: "Divine stratagems probe Heaven's patterns, subtle reckoning exhausts Earth's principles."
translations.idiomatic: Wen De sent a poem: "Divine stratagems probe heaven, subtle reckoning exhausts earth."

sentences.zh: 戰勝功既高，知足願雲止。

translations.literal: "Victory's merit is already high; to know sufficiency is the wish to rest on clouds."
translations.idiomatic: "Your victory is high; knowing enough, rest upon the clouds."

sentences.zh: 」仲文答書諭之，文德燒柵而遁。

translations.literal: Zhongwen answered with a letter instructing him; Wen De burned his palisade and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen answered instructing him; Wen De burned his camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 時宇文述以糧盡欲還，仲文議以精銳追文德，可以有功。

translations.literal: At the time Yuwen Shu, because grain was exhausted, wished to return; Zhongwen argued that with elite troops pursuing Wen De there could be achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu, grain gone, wished to retreat; Zhongwen argued elite pursuit of Wen De could win.

sentences.zh: 述固止之，仲文怒曰：「將軍杖十萬之眾，不能破小賊，何顏以見帝？

translations.literal: Shu firmly stopped him; Zhongwen angrily said: "The general commands a host of a hundred thousand yet cannot break a small bandit—with what face will you see the emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Shu refused; Zhongwen snapped, "You lead a hundred thousand and cannot crush this flea—what face will you show the emperor?"

sentences.zh: 且仲文此行也，固無功矣！

translations.literal: "Moreover this journey of Zhongwen's is certainly without achievement!"
translations.idiomatic: "And this campaign of mine is already ruined!"

sentences.zh: 」述因厲聲曰：「何以知無功？

translations.literal: Shu therefore said in a harsh voice: "How do you know there is no achievement?"
translations.idiomatic: Shu barked, "How do you know there is none?"

sentences.zh: 」仲文曰：「昔周亞夫之為將也，見天子，軍容不變。

translations.literal: Zhongwen said: "In former days when Zhou Yafu was general, he met the Son of Heaven and the army's bearing did not change."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen said, "When Zhou Yafu commanded, he met the Son of Heaven and the army's bearing never shifted."

sentences.zh: 此決在一人，所以功成名遂。

translations.literal: "The outcome rested on one man—therefore merit was established and the name completed."
translations.idiomatic: "Victory hung on one will—therefore fame was made."

sentences.zh: 今者人各其心，何以赴敵？」

translations.literal: "Now each man has his own heart—how can one go to meet the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now every man has his own heart—how can we fight?"

sentences.zh: 初，帝以仲文有計畫，令諸軍諮稟節度，故有此言。

translations.literal: At the beginning the emperor, because Zhongwen had plans, had ordered the armies to consult and follow his command—therefore there was this speech.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had given Zhongwen command over the armies—hence these words.

sentences.zh: 由是述等不得已而從之。

translations.literal: Because of this Shu and the rest had no choice but to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and the rest had no choice but to follow.

sentences.zh: 遂行，東至薩水。

translations.literal: They then marched and eastward reached Sa Water.
translations.idiomatic: They marched east to Sa Water.

sentences.zh: 宇文述以兵餒退歸，師遂敗績。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu because the troops were hungry withdrew and returned; the army then suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu retreated for hunger; the army was ruined.

sentences.zh: 帝以屬吏，諸將皆委罪于仲文。

translations.literal: The emperor handed them to the law officers; the generals all shifted blame onto Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor handed them to the law; every general blamed Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，釋諸將，獨系仲文。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry, released the generals, and alone imprisoned Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, freed the generals, and jailed Zhongwen alone.

sentences.zh: 仲文憂恚發病，困篤，方出之。

translations.literal: Zhongwen, worried and resentful, fell ill; when critically ill he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen, sick with grief, grew desperate; only then was he released.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，時年六十八。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 撰《漢書刊繁》三十卷、《略覽》三十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Abridgment of the Han Dynastic Histories in thirty scrolls and Overview in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Abridgment of the Han Histories in thirty scrolls and Overview in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 有子九人，欽明最知名。

translations.literal: He had nine sons; Qinming was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons; Qinming was best known.

sentences.zh: 寔弟翼，字文若，美風儀，有識度。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Yi, styled Wenruo, had fine bearing and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Yi, styled Wenruo, had grace and judgment.

sentences.zh: 年十一，尚文帝女平原公主，拜員外散騎常侍，封安平縣公。

translations.literal: At eleven he married Emperor Wen's daughter the Princess of Pingyuan, was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and enfeoffed Duke of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he married Emperor Wen's daughter, Princess of Pingyuan, became Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant, and was enfeoffed Duke of Anping.

sentences.zh: 大統十六年，進爵郡公，加大都督，領文帝帳下左右，禁中宿衛。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong he was advanced to commandery duke, made Grand Commander, and attended in Emperor Wen's tent guard, guarding within the palace at night.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year sixteen he was made commandery duke and Grand Commander, guarding Emperor Wen's tent by night.

sentences.zh: 遷武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He became General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 謹平江陵，所賜得軍實，分給諸子。

translations.literal: When Jin pacified Jiangling, what he received from the grants of military goods he divided and gave to his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin took Jiangling, he divided the military spoils among his sons.

sentences.zh: 翼一無所取，唯簡賞口內名望子弟有士風者，別待遇之。

translations.literal: Yi took nothing for himself; he only selected and rewarded by name youths of reputation within his household who had scholar's bearing, treating them separately.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took nothing; he only singled out reputable youths of scholar's bearing in his household and favored them.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞之，賜奴婢二百口，翼固辭不受。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen heard of it he granted two hundred male and female slaves; Yi firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen heard and granted two hundred slaves; Yi firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 尋授車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Opening the Government with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with Opening the Government's ceremonial rank.

sentences.zh: 六官建，除左宮伯。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was dismissed from Left Palace Steward.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were set up, he was removed as Left Palace Steward.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，出為渭州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he went out as Inspector of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended, Yi was sent out as Inspector of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 翼兄寔先蒞此州，頗有惠政。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Shi had earlier come to this province and had quite benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Shi had governed the province before him and left a record of kindness.

sentences.zh: 翼又推誠布信，事存寬簡，夷夏感悅，比之大小馮君焉。

translations.literal: Yi again extended sincerity and spread trust; affairs were kept lenient and simple; barbarians and Chinese alike were moved and pleased, comparing him to the greater and lesser Lords Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi in turn ruled with sincerity and trust, keeping government lenient and spare. Barbarian and Chinese alike rejoiced, likening him to the greater and lesser Lords Feng.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾入寇河右，涼、鄯、河三州咸被攻圍，使來告急。

translations.literal: At the time Tuyuhun invaded the right of the Yellow River; Liang, Shan, and He provinces were all besieged, and envoys came reporting urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun then raided the west bank of the Yellow River. Liang, Shan, and He were all under siege, and urgent dispatches arrived.

sentences.zh: 秦州都督遣翼赴援，不從，寮屬咸以為言。

translations.literal: The Area Commander of Qinzhou sent Yi to go to the rescue; he would not follow, and all the staff spoke against it.
translations.idiomatic: The Area Commander of Qinzhou ordered Yi to relieve them. He refused, and every member of his staff remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 翼曰：「攻取之術，非夷俗所長。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The arts of storming and taking are not what barbarian custom excels at.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Storming walled places is not what these tribes do best.

sentences.zh: 此寇之來，不過鈔掠邊牧耳，安能頓兵城下，久事攻圍！

translations.literal: This band's coming is nothing beyond raiding the border pastures—how could they mass troops below the walls and long pursue siege!
translations.idiomatic: This raid is only border plunder. How could they camp under our walls and sit in a long siege?

sentences.zh: 掠而無獲，勢將自走。

translations.literal: If they raid and gain nothing, the momentum will make them withdraw on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Raid without booty, and they will withdraw of themselves.

sentences.zh: 勞師以往，亦無所及。

translations.literal: To weary the army going there would also accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: To weary our troops marching there would gain us nothing.

sentences.zh: 翼揣之已了，幸勿復言。

translations.literal: Yi had already gauged this to the end—pray do not speak again."
translations.idiomatic: I have already read this through to the end—please say no more."

sentences.zh: 」數日，問至，果如翼所策。

translations.literal: Several days later inquiries arrived, and it was indeed as Yi had strategized.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the reports came in, exactly as Yi had predicted.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭祥討吐谷渾，翼率州兵，先鋒深入，以功增邑。

translations.literal: Helan Xiang attacked Tuyuhun; Yi led the province's troops as vanguard in deep penetration and, for merit, had his fief increased.
translations.idiomatic: When Helan Xiang campaigned against Tuyuhun, Yi led provincial troops as vanguard deep into enemy country and, for merit, received an enlarged fief.

sentences.zh: 尋徵拜右宮伯。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Right Palace Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and made Right Palace Steward.

sentences.zh: 明帝雅愛文史，立麟趾學，在朝有藝業者，不限貴賤，皆聽預焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming greatly loved literature and history; he established the Linqi Academy, and among those at court with artistic accomplishment, without limit of noble or base, all were permitted to join.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming loved letters and history. He founded the Linqi Academy, and every courtier with learning, noble or humble, might attend.

sentences.zh: 乃至蕭捴、王褒等與卑鄙之徒同為學士。

translations.literal: Thus even Xiao Kou, Wang Bao, and others were together scholars with base-born fellows.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xiao Kou, Wang Bao, and others sat as fellows beside men of low birth.

sentences.zh: 翼言於帝曰：「捴，梁之宗子；

translations.literal: Yi spoke to the emperor, saying: "Kou is a clansman of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Yi told the emperor, "Kou is a prince of Liang;

sentences.zh: 褒，梁之公卿，今與趨走同躋，恐非尚賢貴爵之義。

translations.literal: Bao is a grandee of Liang—now to mount the same steps with runners in attendance, I fear this is not the meaning of honoring the worthy and prizing rank."
translations.idiomatic: Bao is a Liang grandee. To share the runners' stair with them is hardly honoring worth and rank."

sentences.zh: 」帝納之，詔翼定其班次，於是有等差矣。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it; an edict ordered Yi to fix their class order, and thereby there were gradations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Yi to set their seating order, and gradations were established.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，翼與晉公護同受遺詔，立武帝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Yi together with Duke of Jin Hu received the testamentary edict and installed Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Yi and Duke of Jin Hu received the deathbed edict and enthroned Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，徙軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding he was transferred to Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year one he became Army Marshal.

sentences.zh: 三年，改封常山郡公。

translations.literal: In the third year he was enfeoffed Duke of Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was enfeoffed Duke of Changshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 天和初，遷司會中大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Accounts, Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianhe he was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Accounts, Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 三年，皇后阿史那氏至自突厥，武帝行親迎之禮，命翼總司儀制。

translations.literal: In the third year the empress of the Ashina clan arrived from the Turks; Emperor Wu performed the ceremony of greeting her in person and ordered Yi to oversee all ritual observances.
translations.idiomatic: In year three the Ashina empress arrived from the Turks. Emperor Wu went out to greet her in person and put Yi in charge of all court ritual.

sentences.zh: 狄人雖蹲踞無節，然咸憚翼之禮法，莫敢違犯。

translations.literal: Though the Di people squatted without decorum, all feared Yi's ritual law and none dared violate it.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Di still squatted without ceremony, they all feared Yi's ritual discipline and dared not break it.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂去職，居喪過禮，為時輩所稱。

translations.literal: He met his father's death and left office; in mourning he exceeded the rites, and his contemporaries praised him.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he left office and mourned beyond the prescribed rites, to the praise of his peers.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔起令視事。

translations.literal: Soon an edict recalled him and ordered him to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict recalled him to duty.

sentences.zh: 武帝又以翼有人倫之鑒，皇太子及諸王等相傅以下，並委翼選置。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also, because Yi had discernment in human relations, entrusted to Yi the selection and placement of the crown prince, all the princes, and those who instructed them and below.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also, trusting Yi's eye for men, entrusted him with choosing tutors and attendants for the crown prince and every prince.

sentences.zh: 其所擢用，皆民譽也，時論僉謂得人。
