translations.literal: Those he raised and employed were all men of popular repute; opinion at the time unanimously said he had found the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Every man he advanced enjoyed public renown, and contemporaries agreed he had chosen well.

sentences.zh: 遷大將軍，總中外宿衛兵事。

translations.literal: He was promoted Grand General and oversaw all inner and outer palace-guard military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand General and commanded all palace guards within and without.

sentences.zh: 晉公護以帝委翼腹心，內懷猜忌，轉為小司徒，加拜柱國。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu, because the emperor entrusted Yi as his intimate, harbored suspicion inwardly; he transferred him to Junior Minister of Education and additionally appointed him Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Hu, seeing the emperor trust Yi as his intimate, grew jealous inwardly. Yi was shifted to Junior Minister of Education with the added title Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 雖外示崇重，實疏斥之。

translations.literal: Though outwardly showing lofty honor, in fact he was pushed aside.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he was honored; in truth he was pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 及誅護，帝召翼，遣往河東取護子中山公訓，仍代鎮蒲州。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, the emperor summoned Yi and sent him to Hedong to take Hu's son Duke of Zhongshan Xun, and he still replaced him in garrisoning Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was killed, the emperor summoned Yi, sent him to Hedong to seize Hu's son Duke of Zhongshan Xun, and left him to hold Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 翼曰：「塚宰無君陵上，自取誅夷。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The Chancellor lacked a lord and overawed his sovereign, and brought execution on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The Chancellor lorded it over his sovereign and earned his own destruction.

sentences.zh: 元惡既除，餘孽宜殄。

translations.literal: Once the chief evil is removed, the remaining spawn ought to be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The chief villain is gone; the remnant brood should be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 然皆陛下骨肉，猶謂疏不間親。

translations.literal: Yet they are all Your Majesty's flesh and blood, and one still says the distant do not come between the near.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they are Your Majesty's own kin, and it is said the distant must not come between the near.

sentences.zh: 陛下不使諸王，而使臣異姓，非直物有橫議，愚臣亦所未安。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not send one of the princes but sends me, a man of another surname, it is not only that the world will have sideways talk—this foolish minister also has not found peace."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends not a prince but me, a man of another surname, the world will murmur—and I myself will not be at ease."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，乃遣越王盛代翼。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and thereupon sent Prince of Yue Sheng to replace Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Prince of Yue Sheng in Yi's place.

sentences.zh: 先是，與齊、陳二境，各修邊防，雖通聘好，而每歲交兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, with Qi and Chen on the two borders, each repaired frontier defenses; though envoys passed with friendly missions, every year there was fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, along the Qi and Chen frontiers each side had strengthened its defenses. Envoys still came with courtesies, yet every year brought battle.

sentences.zh: 然一彼一此，不能有所克獲。

translations.literal: Yet first here, then there, neither could achieve capture or gain.
translations.idiomatic: Victory shifted from side to side, yet neither could win a lasting gain.

sentences.zh: 武帝既親萬機，將圖東討，詔邊城鎮並益儲峙，加戍卒。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu personally handled the myriad affairs, he was about to plan an eastern campaign; he ordered the border towns and garrisons all to increase stored grain and add garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Wu took the reins himself and planned an eastern campaign, he ordered every border town to stock more grain and add garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 二國聞之，亦增修守禦。

translations.literal: The two states heard of it and also increased repair of defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Chen heard of it and strengthened their defenses in turn.

sentences.zh: 翼諫曰：「疆埸相侵，互有勝敗，徒損兵儲，非策之上者。

translations.literal: Yi remonstrated, saying: "On the frontier they invade one another, each having victory and defeat—only soldiers and stores are wasted; this is not the highest policy.
translations.idiomatic: Yi remonstrated: "Border raids trade victories and defeats, but only waste men and grain. That is not the best policy.

sentences.zh: 不若解邊嚴，減兵防，繼好息人，敬待來者。

translations.literal: Better to relax the border alert, reduce troops on defense, renew friendship and let the people rest, and respectfully await those who come.
translations.idiomatic: Better to ease the frontier, cut garrisons, renew friendship, let the people rest, and receive arrivals with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 彼必喜於通和，懈而無備，然後出其不意，一舉而山東可圖。

translations.literal: They will surely delight in communication and peace, slacken and be without defense—then strike from beyond their expectation, and in one move the east of the mountains can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: They will rejoice in peace, grow slack and unready—then strike where they do not expect, and the east of the mountains may be taken at a stroke."

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，出為安州總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande he went out as Area Commander of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year two he went out as Area Commander of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，溳水絕流。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought; the Yu River ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: A great drought struck; the Yu River ran dry.

sentences.zh: 舊俗每逢亢旱，禱白兆山祈雨。

translations.literal: By old custom, whenever there was severe drought, they prayed at Mount Baizhao for rain.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, in severe drought the people prayed for rain at Mount Baizhao.

sentences.zh: 帝先禁群祀，山廟已除。

translations.literal: The emperor had earlier forbidden mass sacrifices; the mountain shrine had already been removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had forbidden mass sacrifices, and the mountain shrine had been torn down.

sentences.zh: 翼遣主簿祭之，即日澍雨。

translations.literal: Yi sent the chief clerk to sacrifice there, and that very day a timely rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent his chief clerk to sacrifice there, and that very day a soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 歲遂有年。

translations.literal: The year thereby had a harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The year brought a harvest.

sentences.zh: 百姓感之，聚會歌舞頌之。

translations.literal: The common people were moved by it; they gathered, sang and danced, and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The people were moved. They gathered, sang, danced, and praised him.

sentences.zh: 四年，武帝將東伐，朝臣未有知者。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Emperor Wu was about to campaign east; the court ministers did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: In year four the emperor planned an eastern campaign, unknown to the court.

sentences.zh: 遣納言盧韞前後三乘驛詣翼問策。

translations.literal: He sent Censor Lu Yun, three times by relay post, to go to Yi and ask his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Censor Lu Yun by relay post, three times in succession, to ask Yi's counsel.

sentences.zh: 翼贊成之。

translations.literal: Yi endorsed and supported it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 及軍出，詔翼自宛，葉趣襄城，旬日下齊一十九城。

translations.literal: When the army marched out, an edict ordered Yi from Wan and Ye to hurry to Xiangcheng; in ten days he took nineteen Qi cities.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched, Yi was ordered from Wan and Ye toward Xiangcheng. In ten days he took nineteen Qi cities.

sentences.zh: 所過秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: Where he passed, not a hair was violated.
translations.idiomatic: Where he passed, not a hair was harmed.

sentences.zh: 所部都督輒入人村，即斬以徇。

translations.literal: If any commander under him entered a village of people, he was immediately beheaded to warn the host.
translations.idiomatic: Any subordinate commander who entered a civilian village was beheaded on the spot as a warning.

sentences.zh: 由是百姓欣悅，赴者如歸。

translations.literal: Thereby the common people were glad and pleased; those who came went as to their home.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced and came to him as to their own home.

sentences.zh: 屬帝有疾，班師，翼亦旋鎮。

translations.literal: Because the emperor fell ill, the army withdrew; Yi also returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell ill and withdrew the army; Yi too returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 轉宜陽總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Area Commander of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Area Commander of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 以宜陽地非襟帶，請移鎮於陝。

translations.literal: Because Yiyang's terrain was not a strategic throat, he requested moving the command to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang was no strategic choke point; he asked to move headquarters to Shan.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，仍除陝州刺史，總管如舊。

translations.literal: The edict followed him; he was still made Inspector of Shan Prefecture, Area Commander as before.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted it. He was made Inspector of Shan while keeping the area command.

sentences.zh: 其年，大軍復東討，翼自陝入，徑到洛陽。

translations.literal: That year the great army again campaigned east; Yi entered from Shan and went straight to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That year the main army campaigned east again. Yi entered from Shan and went straight to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 齊洛州刺史獨孤承業開門降，河南九州三十鎮，一時俱下。

translations.literal: Qi Governor of Luoyang Dugu Chengye opened the gates and surrendered; the nine provinces and thirty garrisons of Henan all fell at once.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's Governor of Luoyang Dugu Chengye opened the gates and surrendered. Nine provinces and thirty Henan garrisons fell at once.

sentences.zh: 襄城人庶等喜復見翼，並壺漿道左。

translations.literal: The people of Xiangcheng and so on were glad to see Yi again and all set out pots of drink by the road to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xiangcheng rejoiced to see Yi again and lined the road with pots of drink.

sentences.zh: 除河陽總管，仍徙豫州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Area Commander of Heyang and still transferred to Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Area Commander of Heyang, then transferred to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳將魯天念久圍光州，聞翼到汝南，望風退散。

translations.literal: Chen general Lu Tiannian had long besieged Guang Prefecture; hearing Yi had reached Runan, he scattered before the wind and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chen general Lu Tiannian had long besieged Guang Prefecture. When he heard Yi had reached Runan, he broke camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 大象初，徵拜大司徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang he was summoned and appointed Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Daxiang he was recalled and made Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 詔翼巡長城，立亭鄣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yi to tour the Long Wall and establish beacon towers and border posts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yi to tour the Long Wall and set up beacon towers and border posts.

sentences.zh: 西自雁門，東至碣石，創新改舊，咸得其要害。

translations.literal: From Yanmen in the west to Jieshi in the east, whether newly built or old and altered, all obtained their strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: From Yanmen in the west to Jieshi in the east, whether newly built or old and refitted, every post sat on a key point.

sentences.zh: 仍除幽州總管。

translations.literal: He was still made Area Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Area Commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，突厥屢為抄掠，居人失業。

translations.literal: Earlier the Turks had repeatedly raided and plundered; the inhabitants lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Turks had raided again and again, and the people lost their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 翼素有威武，兼明斥候，自是不敢犯塞，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Yi had long possessed martial awe and was also skilled in reconnaissance; from then on they did not dare violate the frontier passes, and the common people were secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had long held martial awe and knew reconnaissance. From then on they dared not cross the passes, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥據相州舉兵，以書招翼。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong held Xiang Prefecture and raised troops, he sent a letter to recruit Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong seized Xiang Prefecture and rebelled, he wrote to win Yi over.

sentences.zh: 翼執其使，並書送之。

translations.literal: Yi seized his envoy and, together with the letter, sent them on.
translations.idiomatic: Yi seized the envoy and forwarded him with the letter.

sentences.zh: 時隋文帝執政，賜翼雜繒一千五百段，並珍寶服玩等。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wen of Sui held the government; he bestowed on Yi fifteen hundred lengths of mixed silks, together with treasures, robes, and playthings.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian then held power. He gave Yi fifteen hundred lengths of mixed silk, with treasures, robes, and fine objects.

sentences.zh: 進位上柱國，封任國公，增邑通前五千戶，別食任城縣一千戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Senior Pillar of State, enfeoffed Duke of Ren state, with fief households totaling five thousand together with earlier grants; separately he received the tax revenue of Rencheng county, one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed Duke of Ren, five thousand households in all with earlier grants. He separately received the tax of Rencheng county, one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 翼又遣子讓通表勸進，並請入朝，許之。

translations.literal: Yi also sent his son Rang with a memorial urging accession and also requested to enter court; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also sent his son Rang with a memorial urging Yang Jian to take the throne and asked leave to come to court; both were granted.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，翼入朝，上降榻握手極歡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang, Yi entered court; the emperor descended from the couch, took his hand, and was exceedingly glad.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Kaihuang, Yi came to court. The emperor stepped down from the couch, took his hand, and rejoiced exceedingly.

sentences.zh: 數日，拜太尉。

translations.literal: Several days later he was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 或有告翼往在幽州，欲同尉遲迥。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Yi, when formerly in Youzhou, had wished to join Yuchi Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Yi, while in Youzhou, had meant to join Yuchi Jiong.

sentences.zh: 按驗，以無實見原。

translations.literal: On investigation there was no fact; he was forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation found no truth in it, and he was forgiven.

sentences.zh: 三年，薨於本位。

translations.literal: In the third year he died in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he died in office.

sentences.zh: 加贈六州諸軍事、蒲州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Commander over the armies of six provinces and Inspector of Pu Prefecture; posthumous name Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made commander over six provinces' armies and Inspector of Pu, with posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 翼性恭儉，與物無競，常以滿盈自戒，故能以功名終。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was respectful and frugal; he contended with nothing; he constantly took fullness as a warning to himself—therefore he could end with merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was respectful and frugal and contended with no one. He constantly warned himself against fullness, and so ended his days in merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 子璽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 璽字伯符，少有器幹。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Bofu, in youth had capacity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, styled Bofu, showed talent and resolve early.

sentences.zh: 仕周，位職方中大夫，封黎陽縣公。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as Director of the Masters of Equipage, Grand Master, and was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he was Director of the Masters of Equipage, Grand Master, and Duke of Liyang county.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，轉右勳曹中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was transferred to Director of the Right Merit Bureau, Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he became Director of the Right Merit Bureau, Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 尋領右忠義。

translations.literal: Soon he also led the Right Righteousness Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also commanded the Right Righteousness Guard.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，加上大將軍，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was given the additional title Grand General and advanced in rank to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Xi was made Grand General and advanced to a commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 曆汴、邵二州刺史，所曆並有恩惠。

translations.literal: He successively served as Inspector of Bian and Shao, and in every post he had kindness and favor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Inspector of Bian and Shao in turn, and in each post showed kindness.

sentences.zh: 後檢校江陵總管，邵州人張願等數十人詣闕上表，請留璽。

translations.literal: Later, as acting Area Commander of Jiangling, several tens of men of Shao Prefecture, Zhang Yuan and others, went to the palace gate with a memorial requesting Xi be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as acting Area Commander of Jiangling, several dozen men of Shao, led by Zhang Yuan, petitioned at the palace gate to keep Xi.

sentences.zh: 上嘉歎良久，令還邵州，父老相賀。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in admiration a long while and ordered him back to Shao; the elders congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed long in admiration and sent him back to Shao. The elders congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 尋曆洛、熊二州刺史，亦粗有惠政。

translations.literal: Soon he successively served as Inspector of Luo and Xiong; he also had rough kindness in government.
translations.idiomatic: He soon held Luo and Xiong in turn and showed a rough but genuine kindness in office.

sentences.zh: 以疾還京師，卒於家，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: Because of illness he returned to the capital and died at home; posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Illness brought him back to the capital; he died at home, posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 有子志本。

translations.literal: He had a son Zhiben.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Zhiben.

sentences.zh: 璽弟詮，位上儀同三司、吏部下大夫、常山公。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Quan held the posts Senior Colonel of the Third Rank, Junior Minister of Personnel, and Duke of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Quan was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank, Junior Minister of Personnel, and Duke of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 詮弟讓，儀同三司。

translations.literal: Quan's younger brother Rang was Colonel of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's younger brother Rang was Colonel of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 翼弟義。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Yi.

sentences.zh: 義字慈恭，少矜嚴，有操尚，篤志好學。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Cigong, in youth was stern and dignified, had moral resolve, and with deep will loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Cigong, was stern and dignified in youth, principled, and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 大統末，以父功賜爵平昌縣伯。

translations.literal: At the end of Great Dominion, through his father's merit he was granted the rank Baron of Pingchang county.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Great Dominion he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingchang for his father's merit.

sentences.zh: 後改封廣都縣公。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed Duke of Guangdu county.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Duke of Guangdu county.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝踐阼，遷安武太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, he was promoted Governor of Anwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended, he became Governor of Anwu.

sentences.zh: 專崇教化，不尚威刑。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to promoting transformation and did not esteem punitive law.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to civilizing the people and did not rely on harsh punishments.

sentences.zh: 有郡人張善安、王叔兒爭財相訟，義曰：「太守德薄不勝所致。

translations.literal: There were men of the commandery, Zhang Shan'an and Wang Shuer, who disputed property and sued one another; Yi said: "This comes from the prefect's thin virtue and inability to bear up.
translations.idiomatic: Two men of the commandery, Zhang Shan'an and Wang Shuer, sued one another over property. Yi said, "This comes from the prefect's thin virtue and failure to bear the weight of office.

sentences.zh: 」於是以家財分與二人，喻而遣去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took his household wealth and divided it between the two men, instructed them, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: " He took his own household wealth, divided it between them, admonished them, and dismissed the case.

sentences.zh: 善安等各懷恥愧，移貫他州。

translations.literal: Shan'an and the others each harbored shame; they moved their household registers to other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Shan'an and the others were shamed into moving their households to other provinces.

sentences.zh: 於是風化大洽。

translations.literal: Thereby customs were greatly harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were thereby greatly harmonized.

sentences.zh: 進封建平郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed Duke of Jianping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced and enfeoffed Duke of Jianping commandery.

sentences.zh: 明、武世，曆西兗、瓜、邵三州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eras of Ming and Wu he successively served as Inspector of Xi Yan, Gua, and Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ming and Wu he held Xi Yan, Gua, and Shao in turn.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，進位開府。

translations.literal: Several times he followed in campaigns and was advanced to Opening Office, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He followed several campaigns and was advanced to Opening Office, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，政刑日亂，義上疏諫帝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, government and punishments daily fell into disorder; Yi submitted a memorial remonstrating the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, law and punishment grew daily more chaotic. Yi submitted a memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 時鄭譯、劉昉以恩幸當權。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Yi and Liu Fang, through favor and intimacy, held power.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi and Liu Fang then held power through imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 謂義不利於己，先惡之於帝。

translations.literal: They said Yi's words were not to their benefit and first spoke ill of him to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They said Yi's words harmed them and first slandered him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝覽表色動，謂侍臣曰：「於義謗訕朝廷也。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and his color changed; he said to the attending ministers: "Yi is slandering the court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, his face changed, and he told the attendants, "Yi is slandering the court."

sentences.zh: 」禦正大夫顏之儀進曰：「古先哲王立謗訕之木，置敢諫之鼓，猶懼不聞過。

translations.literal: Correcting Master of the Left Yan Zhiyi advanced and said: "The ancient sage kings set up a post for slander and hung a drum for bold remonstrance, yet still feared not hearing their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Correcting Master of the Left Yan Zhiyi stepped forward: "Ancient sage kings set up a post for slander and a drum for bold remonstrance, yet still feared never hearing their faults.

sentences.zh: 於義之言，不可罪也。

translations.literal: Yi's words cannot be made a crime."
translations.idiomatic: Yi's words cannot be punished."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon released the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 及王謙構逆，隋文帝謀將于高熲，熲言義可為元帥。

translations.literal: When Wang Qian raised rebellion, Emperor Wen of Sui was planning to use Gao Jiong as commander; Jiong said Yi could serve as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian rebelled, Yang Jian meant to make Gao Jiong commander. Jiong said Yi could lead the army.

sentences.zh: 文帝將任之，劉昉曰：「梁睿任望素重，不可居義下。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to appoint him, but Liu Fang said: "Liang Rui's standing and hope have long been weighty—he cannot stand below Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was about to appoint him, but Liu Fang said, "Liang Rui's standing is too great to serve under Yi."

sentences.zh: 」乃以睿為元帥，義為行軍總管，將左軍，破謙將達奚惎於開遠。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rui was made commander-in-chief and Yi made Campaigning Area Commander, commanding the left army; he defeated Qian's general Daxi Ji at Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was made commander-in-chief instead, with Yi as Campaigning Area Commander leading the left wing. He defeated Qian's general Daxi Ji at Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 尋拜潼州總管，賜奴婢五百口，雜采三千段，超拜上柱國。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Area Commander of Tong Prefecture, granted five hundred slaves and concubines and three thousand lengths of mixed silks, and leap-promoted Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Area Commander of Tong, granted five hundred slaves and concubines and three thousand lengths of mixed silk, and leap-promoted Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾免歸，卒于京師。

translations.literal: After more than a year, because of illness he was relieved and returned; he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year illness relieved him of office. He returned and died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 贈豫州刺史，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Inspector of Yu Prefecture; posthumous name Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was Inspector of Yu, posthumous name Gang.

sentences.zh: 子宣道、宣敏，並知名。

translations.literal: He had sons Xuandao and Xuanmin, both of known name.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Xuandao and Xuanmin, both well known.

sentences.zh: 宣道字元明，性謹密，不交非類。

translations.literal: Xuandao, styled Yuanming, by nature was careful and close; he did not associate with unworthy sorts.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandao, styled Yuanming, was careful and reserved and kept no unworthy company.

sentences.zh: 仕周，以父功，賜爵城安縣男，位小承禦上士。

translations.literal: He served Zhou; through his father's merit he was granted the rank Baron of Cheng'an county, and held the post Junior Bearer of the Imperial Carriage, Senior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou, for his father's merit, he was Baron of Cheng'an and Junior Bearer of the Imperial Carriage, Senior Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，引為外兵曹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, he was brought in as Outer Master of Troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was Chancellor, Xuandao was brought in as Outer Master of Troops.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，遷內史舍人，進爵為子。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he was promoted Palace Scribe and advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Xuandao became Palace Scribe and was advanced to Viscount.

sentences.zh: 父憂，水漿不入口者累日。

translations.literal: In his father's mourning he did not take water or broth for many days.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his father he took neither water nor broth for many days.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起令視事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled and ordered to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was recalled to duty.

sentences.zh: 免喪，拜車騎將軍，兼右衛長史，舍人如故。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and concurrently Right Guard Chief Commandant, Palace Scribe as before.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Right Guard Chief Commandant, retaining his post as Palace Scribe.

sentences.zh: 後遷太子左衛副率，進位上儀同。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted Deputy Commandant of the Crown Prince's Left Guard and advanced to Senior Colonel of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was later Deputy Commandant of the Crown Prince's Left Guard and Senior Colonel of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子志甯，早知名。

translations.literal: His son Zhiyu was early of known name.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiyu was known early.

sentences.zh: 出繼叔父宣敏。

translations.literal: He went out to succeed his uncle Xuanmin.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to succeed his uncle Xuanmin.

sentences.zh: 宣敏字仲達，少沈密，有才思。

translations.literal: Xuanmin, styled Zhongda, in youth was deep and close, with literary talent and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmin, styled Zhongda, was deep and reserved in youth, with literary talent and purpose.

sentences.zh: 年十一，詣周趙王招，命之賦詩。

translations.literal: At age eleven he went to Prince of Zhao Zhao's residence; Zhao ordered him to compose a poem.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he visited Prince of Zhao Zhao, who ordered him to compose a poem.

sentences.zh: 宣敏為詩，甚有幽貞之志。

translations.literal: Xuanmin composed the poem, with very much the will of secluded integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmin's poem breathed secluded integrity.

sentences.zh: 招大奇之，坐客莫不嗟賞。

translations.literal: Zhao was greatly struck by it; seated guests none did not sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao marveled at it; every guest present sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 起家右侍上士，遷千牛備身。

translations.literal: He began his career as Right Attendant Senior Gentleman and was promoted Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Right Attendant Senior Gentleman and was promoted Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐阼，拜奉車都尉，奉使撫慰巴、蜀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and sent as envoy to comfort Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Xuanmin was Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and sent to comfort Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 及還，上疏曰：

translations.literal: When he returned, he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On his return he submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞開磐石之宗，漢室於是惟永；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that by opening the bedrock lineage the house of Han was thereby long enduring;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that by opening the bedrock lineage the house of Han endured;

sentences.zh: 建維城之固，周祚所以靈長。

translations.literal: by establishing the secure rampart-city the fortune of Zhou was thereby numinous and long.
translations.idiomatic: by establishing the secure rampart-city the fortune of Zhou remained numinous and long.

sentences.zh: 昔秦皇置牧守而罷諸侯，魏後昵謟邪而疏骨肉，遂使宗社移於他族，神器傳於異姓。

translations.literal: In former times the First Emperor of Qin set pasture governors and abolished the feudal lords; the Wei of Later Han doted on flattering villains and kept kin at a distance—thereby the altars of state shifted to another clan and the sacred vessel passed to another surname.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's First Emperor set pasture governors and abolished the feudal lords; Later Han doted on flatterers and kept kin at a distance—so the altars passed to another clan and the sacred vessel to another surname.

sentences.zh: 此事之明，甚於觀火。

translations.literal: This matter's clarity is brighter than watching fire.
translations.idiomatic: This lesson is clearer than watching fire.

sentences.zh: 然山川設險，非親勿居。

translations.literal: Yet mountains and rivers set their barriers—none but kin should dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Yet mountains and rivers set their barriers, and none but kin should hold them.

sentences.zh: 且蜀土沃饒，人物殷阜，西通邛、僰，南屬荊、巫。

translations.literal: Moreover the soil of Shu is fertile and rich, its people numerous and flourishing; west it connects with Qiong and Bo, south it belongs to Jing and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's soil is rich, its people numerous; west it reaches Qiong and Bo, south it joins Jing and Wu.

sentences.zh: 周德之衰，茲土遂成戎首；

translations.literal: When Zhou's virtue declined, this land thereupon became the head of the barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou's virtue declined, this land became the barbarians' head;

sentences.zh: 炎政失禦，此地便為禍先。

translations.literal: when Yan's government lost control, this place then became the source of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: when the Han house lost its grip, this place became disaster's source.

sentences.zh: 是以明者防于無形，安者制其未亂，方可慶隆萬世，年逾七百。

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened guard before form appears, and the secure control what is not yet in disorder—only then can one celebrate grandeur for ten thousand generations and exceed seven hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened guard before form appears; the secure control disorder before it rises—only then may fortune celebrate ten thousand generations and exceed seven hundred years.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下日角龍顏，膺樂推之運；

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's sun-corner and dragon-countenance, bearing the fortune of the people's pushing upward;
translations.idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty's heaven-marked brow and dragon face, bearing the fortune of the people's upward push;

sentences.zh: 參天貳地，居揖讓之期。

translations.literal: matching heaven and assisting earth, occupying the season of yielding and yielding up.
translations.idiomatic: matching heaven and assisting earth, in the season of yielding the throne.

sentences.zh: 億兆宅心，百神受職。

translations.literal: The hundred million fix their hearts; the hundred spirits receive their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred million fix their hearts; the hundred spirits receive their offices.

sentences.zh: 理須樹建籓屏，封植子孫，繼周、漢之宏圖，改秦、魏之覆軌。

translations.literal: It is right to plant and establish the screen of the realm, enfeoff and nurture sons and grandsons, continue the great design of Zhou and Han, and alter the overturned track of Qin and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: It is right to plant the realm's screen, enfeoff and nurture sons and grandsons, continue Zhou and Han's great design, and turn from Qin and Wei's overturned path.

sentences.zh: 抑近習之權勢，崇公族之本枝。

translations.literal: Restrain the power of near intimates and exalt the root branches of the ducal clan.
translations.idiomatic: Restrain near favorites' power and exalt the ducal clan's root branches.

sentences.zh: 但三蜀、二齊，古稱天險，分王戚屬，今正其時。

translations.literal: But the Three Shus and the Two Qis are anciently called heaven's barriers—to divide them among kingly kin, now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Shus and Two Qis are anciently called heaven's barriers—to enfeoff kingly kin there is no better time.

sentences.zh: 若使利建合宜，封樹得所，則巨猾息其非望，奸臣杜其邪謀。

translations.literal: If the profitable establishment is fitting and the enfeoffment and planting obtain their places, then great villains will quiet their improper hopes and treacherous ministers will stop their crooked plots.
translations.idiomatic: If establishment is fitting and enfeoffment well placed, great villains will quiet their improper hopes and treacherous ministers stop their crooked plots.

sentences.zh: 盛業洪基，同天地之長久；

translations.literal: The flourishing enterprise and great foundation will share heaven and earth in long endurance;
translations.idiomatic: The flourishing enterprise and great foundation will share heaven and earth in long endurance;

sentences.zh: 英聲茂實，齊日月之照臨。

translations.literal: splendid fame and lush achievement will equal sun and moon in shining down.
translations.idiomatic: splendid fame and lush achievement will equal sun and moon in shining down.

sentences.zh: 臣雖學謝多聞，然情深體國，輒申管見，戰灼惟深。

translations.literal: Your servant, though his learning falls short of much hearing, yet his feeling is deep and his body is for the state—I venture this tube-and-bamboo view, trembling and scorched in the utmost depth."
translations.idiomatic: Though my learning falls short of wide hearing, my feeling runs deep for the state. I venture this narrow view, trembling with the utmost fear."

sentences.zh: 帝省表嘉之，謂高熲曰：「於氏世有人焉。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and praised it; he said to Gao Jiong: "The Yu house for generations has had such men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with praise and told Gao Jiong, "The Yu house for generations has produced such men."

sentences.zh: 」竟納其言，遣蜀王秀鎮於蜀。

translations.literal: He finally accepted his words and sent Prince of Shu Xiu to garrison Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He finally accepted the advice and sent Prince of Shu Xiu to hold Shu.

sentences.zh: 宣敏常以盛滿之誡，昔賢所重，每懷靜退。

translations.literal: Xuanmin constantly took the warning of fullness as the caution of former worthies valued; he always harbored the wish for quiet withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmin constantly heeded the warning against fullness that former worthies prized and longed for quiet withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 著《述志賦》以見志焉。

translations.literal: He composed "Rhapsody on Stating My Will" to show his aim.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the "Rhapsody on Stating My Will" to declare his intent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官，年二十九。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office, age twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office, aged twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 義弟禮，上將軍、趙州刺史、安平郡公。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Li was Senior General, Inspector of Zhao Prefecture, and Duke of Anping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Li was Senior General, Inspector of Zhao, and Duke of Anping commandery.

sentences.zh: 禮弟智，初為開府。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Zhi at first was Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: Li's younger brother Zhi at first held Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 以受宣帝密旨，告齊王憲反，遂封齊國公。

translations.literal: Because he received Emperor Xuan's secret order, he reported Prince of Qi Xian's rebellion; he was thereupon enfeoffed Duke of Qi state.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Emperor Xuan's secret order, he reported Prince of Qi Xian for rebellion and was enfeoffed Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 尋拜柱國，位大司空。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Pillar of State and held the post Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon Pillar of State and Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 智弟紹，上開府、綏州刺史、華陽郡公。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Shao was Senior Opening Office, Inspector of Sui Prefecture, and Duke of Huayang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Shao was Senior Opening Office, Inspector of Sui, and Duke of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 紹弟弼，上儀同、平恩縣公。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Bi was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank and Duke of Ping'en county.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's younger brother Bi was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank and Duke of Ping'en county.

sentences.zh: 弼弟蘭，上儀同、襄陽縣開國公。

translations.literal: Bi's younger brother Lan was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank and Duke who founded Xiangyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's younger brother Lan was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank and founding Duke of Xiangyang county.

sentences.zh: 蘭弟曠，上儀同。

translations.literal: Lan's younger brother Kuang was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's younger brother Kuang was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 贈恆州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Inspector of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was Inspector of Heng.

sentences.zh: 論曰：魏氏平定中原，于栗磾有武功於三世。

translations.literal: Discussion says: When the house of Wei pacified the central plains, Yu Lidi had military achievement through three reigns.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: When Wei pacified the central plains, Yu Lidi won military merit through three reigns.

sentences.zh: 兼以虛己下物，罰不濫加，斯亦諸將所稀矣。

translations.literal: Together with emptying himself to place himself below others and punishments not recklessly applied, this too is rare among the generals.
translations.idiomatic: He also emptied himself before others and did not punish recklessly—rare among generals even then.

sentences.zh: 洛拔任參內外，以功名自終。

translations.literal: Luoba took charge within and without and ended with merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Luoba took charge within and without and ended in merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 烈氣概沈遠。

translations.literal: Lie by spirit and bearing was deep and far.
translations.idiomatic: Lie was deep and far in spirit and bearing.

sentences.zh: 受任艱危之際，有柱石之質，殆禦侮之臣乎！

translations.literal: Receiving appointment in a time of peril and danger, he had the substance of a pillar stone—perhaps a minister to repel insult!
translations.idiomatic: Trusted in peril's hour, he had a pillar's substance—perhaps a minister to repel insult!

sentences.zh: 忠以梗樸見親，乘非其據，遂擅威權，生殺自已。

translations.literal: Zhong was seen as close for his blunt simplicity; riding what was not his to hold, he thereupon monopolized awesome power, life and death at his own will.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong won favor through blunt simplicity, then seized power not his to hold and made life and death his own.

sentences.zh: 苟非女主之世，何以全其門族？

translations.literal: If it had not been the era of an empress, how could the gate and clan have been preserved whole?
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been an empress's age, how could his house have survived whole?

sentences.zh: 不至誅滅，抑其幸也。

translations.literal: That he did not reach extermination and punishment was also his luck.
translations.idiomatic: That he escaped extermination was luck as much as merit.

sentences.zh: 謹負佐時之略，逢興運之期，為大廈之棟樑，擬巨川之舟楫。

translations.literal: Jin bore the strategy of assisting the age; he met the season of rising fortune, was a rafter beam for the great hall, likened to the boat and oar on the great stream.
translations.idiomatic: Jin bore the strategy of assisting his age, met a rising fortune, was rafter beam to the great hall and boat on the great stream.

sentences.zh: 卒以耆年碩德，譽高望重。

translations.literal: He ended with venerable years and great virtue, reputation high and hope weighty.
translations.idiomatic: He ended in venerable years and great virtue, his reputation high and his hope weighty.

sentences.zh: 禮備上庠，功歌司樂。

translations.literal: Rites were complete in the upper school; merit was sung in the Director of Music.
translations.idiomatic: Rites were complete in the upper school; his merit was sung in the Director of Music.

sentences.zh: 而常以滿盈為誡，覆折是憂，不有君子，何以能國。

translations.literal: Yet he constantly took fullness as a warning and feared overturn and break—without a gentleman, how could the state stand?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he constantly warned himself against fullness and feared overturn—without such a gentleman, how could the state stand?

sentences.zh: 翼既功臣之子，地則姻親，荷累葉之恩，兼文武之寄，理同休戚，與存與亡。

translations.literal: Yi was both son of a meritorious minister and by position a marriage kinsman; he bore favor through successive generations and together held civil and martial trust—principle was the same as sharing weal and woe, surviving and perishing together.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was son of a meritorious minister and a marriage kinsman by position. Favor piled through generations; civil and martial trust rested on him together—his fate was bound to the throne's.

sentences.zh: 加以總戎馬之權，受扞城之托，智能足以衛難，勢力足以勤王。

translations.literal: Added to this, he held overall authority over war horses and received the entrustment of defending the walls; intelligence and ability were enough to guard against peril, power and force enough to stir the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: He held overall command of armies and the trust of defending the realm. Wit enough to guard peril, power enough to stir the royal house.

sentences.zh: 曾無釋位之心，但務隨時之義。

translations.literal: He never had the heart to release his post, but only pursued the meaning of following the time.
translations.idiomatic: He never showed a heart to release his post, only the art of following the time.

sentences.zh: 弘名節以高貴，豈所望於斯人！

translations.literal: To exalt name and integrity in order to be noble and honored—is that what one hoped from such a man!
translations.idiomatic: To exalt integrity and win honor—is that all one could ask of such a man!

sentences.zh: 仲文博涉書記，以英略自許，尉迥之亂，遂立功名。

translations.literal: Zhongwen was broadly versed in documents and records and with heroic strategy made himself his own measure; in Yuchi Jiong's disorder he thereupon established merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen was versed in documents and records and measured himself by heroic strategy. In Yuchi Jiong's rebellion he won merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，屢當推穀。

translations.literal: From then on afterward, several times he was placed at the hub of command.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he several times held the army's hub.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，實喪師徒。

translations.literal: The Liaodong campaign in fact lost army and followers.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong campaign in fact lost army and followers.

sentences.zh: 斯乃大樹將顛，蓋非一繩之罪也。

translations.literal: This was the great tree about to topple—it was not the fault of a single rope alone.
translations.idiomatic: The great tree was already toppling—it was not the fault of one rope alone.

sentences.zh: 義運屬時來，宣其力用，崇基弗墜，析薪克荷，盛矣！

translations.literal: Yi's fortune met the time's coming; Xuandao and Xuanmin displayed their strength— the lofty foundation did not fall, split firewood could be borne—how flourishing!
translations.idiomatic: Yi's fortune met the time's coming; Xuandao and Xuanmin showed their strength—the lofty foundation did not fall, split firewood could be borne. How flourishing!
